articleTitle: Side Lobe and Side Band Reduction of Time Modulated Circular Antenna Array Using Novel Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to design 16-elements time modulated asymmetric circular antenna array (TMASCAA) for optimum far-field radiation pattern synthesis. By minimizing the sidelobe levels (SLLs), the far-field radiation pattern is designed to minimize the interference of TMASCAA. For achieving the ultra-low SLLs, an optimal combination of switch-ON time sequence and progressive phase delay is determined using a proposed meta-heuristics technique which is novel particle swarm optimization (NPSO). TMASCAA is also considered for the practical antenna at fundamental frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>= 2.4 GHz to calculate sideband levels (SBLs), feed network efficiency, and directivity using the NPSO technique.

articleTitle: Tunable UWB/Narrowband Terahertz Metasurface Absorber Through Controlled Relaxation Time
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work presents the design of a polarization-insensitive graphene-based tunable metasurface absorber (TMSA) for a terahertz (THz) regime. The TMSA can provide ultra-wide and narrowband absorptivity response by properly selecting the relaxation time value <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\tau)$</tex> before fabrication. The TMSA provides a bandwidth (BW) of 193.4% with absorptivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(A(f))\geq 90\%$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau=0.06$</tex> ps. At the same time, an absorption BW of 6.86% could be achieved from the same design by selecting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau=1$</tex> ps. The thickness of ultrathin TMSA is only 3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, corresponding to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{g}/638.87$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{g}$</tex> is guided wavelength computed at 0.1 THz. The periodicity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda_{g}/191.66)$</tex> of TMSA is also quite less to ensure effective homogeneity condition. The absorber works well under both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarizations for wide incidence angle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\theta)$</tex>. TMSA provide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A(f)\geq$</tex> 90 % for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta\leq 60^{\circ}$</tex> when working as UWB absorber and provide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A(f)\geq 75\%$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta\leq 60^{\circ}$</tex> when working as narrowband absorber. TMSA also provides a shift in the absorption peak from 3.5 to 6.2 THz by varying chemical potential <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mu_{c})$</tex> from 0.3 to 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{eV}$</tex> when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tau$</tex> is kept fixed at 1 ps.

articleTitle: Real-Time Beehive Condition Improving Frequency Selection and Bee Welfare Monitoring and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Beekeeping is a crucial agricultural activity that is needed for pollination and the production of honey. For bee colonies to remain healthy and productive, ideal hive conditions must be maintained. In this study, a real-time hive condition management system is described for beekeepers based on IoT. An ESP8266 microcontroller, a DHT11 sensor for measuring temperature and humidity, and a buzzer are all components of our system. We have collected and evaluated temperature and humidity data from beehives over a long period of time by deploying our monitoring system. We go over our system's practical applications for beekeeping, such as the early identification of unfavorable environmental circumstances and the avoidance of hive stress. We recognize some issues that need additional adjustment, such as sensor accuracy and power supply. This research presents an approach for beekeepers looking to enhance hive management techniques and contributes to the expanding field of IoT in agriculture.

articleTitle: Parking Wireless Assistive System for Smart City Parking Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Effective and shrewd parking management is essential in the 21st century's congested environments. The creation and deployment of a Smart Parking Assist system using the ESP8266 module & Blynk cloud platform are described. The system seeks to lessen the difficulties associated with parking. The system monitors parking space availability and aids drivers in directing their automobiles into allocated locations using ultrasonic sensors, LED displays, and servo motors. The methodology, system architecture, and the integration of multiple components are all thoroughly covered. The outcomes of our implementation are given and assessed, including information on parking space availability and system performance. Additionally, the talk covers the significance of this initiative in relation to IoT and smart city applications, addressing potential uses & advantages. This Smart Parking Assist system demonstrates how IoT solutions may reduce traffic congestion, and support effective mobility.

articleTitle: Re-Configurable Bi-Functional Meta-Surface Based Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a re-configurable bi-functional meta-surface for polarization conversion is designed and verified. The structure consists of a split ring resonator (SRR) with metal strips on the middle of each side. To make it re-configurable PIN diodes are incorporated. The proposed meta-surface offers a dual function in the OFF state of PIN diodes. It functions as linear to linear polarization converter over the frequency range 4.92GHz to 7.06GHz and a linear to circular polarization converter over the frequency range 8.4GHz to 9.4GHz. In the ON state, it functions as a metal reflector. The bias lines for the RF switches are also included in the structure. An axial ratio (AR) of below 3dB is obtained for an incident angle uptill 10°. A PCR value of 1 is also obtained up to the incident angle of 10°.

articleTitle: Slot Loaded Offset Feed SIW Cavity Backed Triangular Perturbed Antenna with Improved Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This article describes a new technique for enhancing the bandwidth of substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-supported slot antennas with symmetrical triangular perturbed cavities. One way the cavity-backed antenna feeding method has been modified is by employing offset feeding of a microstrip line and a transition from the microstrip to the grounded coplanar waveguide. This helps to excite the TE120 mode in the cavity while increasing the impedance matching to the slot antenna. The proposed antenna has a resonant frequency of 10.4 GHz, a bandwidth of 4.3%, a gain of 5.54 dBi, a front-to-back ratio of 10.6 dB, and a maximum cross-polarization level of −30 dB. It is designed to operate in the X band (8–12 GHz) applications.

articleTitle: A FSS- based Single Layer Reflective Polarizer for X/Ku- Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The paper discusses a FSS- based single-layer reflection type linear to circular polarization converter that offers angular stability and a high energy conversion ratio. The design converts linearly polarized waves to left circularly polarized waves in the frequency ranges of 8.16-8.36 GHz and 13.5-13.8 GHz, while the reflected wave is right circularly polarized in the frequency range of 9.3-11.3 GHz. The axial ratio is less than 3 dB for TE and TM modes up to 45° over above mentioned frequency ranges except 8.16-8.36 GHz. The unit cell periodicity is 8.8 mm or 0.24 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\lambda }_0}$</tex> , where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\lambda }_0}$</tex> represents the wavelength at the center frequency of the lowest frequency range and has a total thickness of 1.625 mm (0.046 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\lambda }_0}$</tex> ). Further, a prototype has been fabricated and tested for the proof-of-the concept. The measured results found to be in good agreement with simulated results. The proposed reflective polarizer can be used for satellite communications in X/Ku bands.

articleTitle: Dual-band E-Textile Artificial Magnetic Conductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents an E-textile artificial magnetic conductor design using Jeans and Pure Copper Polyester taffeta fabric material. The proposed dual-band geometry is designed as square rings and strip structures with different lengths of unit cell on 20mm × 20mm dimensions. The proposed E-textile AMC provides the reflection phase frequencies at 2.45 GHz and 5.2 GHz with a ±90° reflection phase. Also, the parametric study shows reflection phase does not change with different polarization angles and oblique incident angles.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Rat-Race Coupler for 5G MIMO Antenna System Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work, design and analysis of a rat race coupler (RRC) for 5G MIMO systems operating at 3.5 GHz. The RRC and rectangular patch array MIMO antenna design are utilized for transmitter and receiver applications. That enables 5G operation. The three components of the proposed antenna are constructed using a traditional rectangular patch antenna and linked in series with a quarter wave feed line and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50 \Omega$</tex> impedance line. The same array antenna is used to build a two-port MIMO antenna that operates at a frequency of 3.5 GHz. It provides a compact size, excellent isolation, and low insertion loss, making it an ideal solution. The coupler, measuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$32.6\times 33.2 \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>, provides a minimum reflection rate of −3 dB, a return loss of over −30 dB, an isolation loss of less than −20 dB, and an excellent coupling coefficient. The antenna has the gain of 5.5 dBi, a return loss of 30 dB, and a bidirectional pattern and isolation of more than −20 dB. The proposed work can be used in 5G MIMO system applications.

articleTitle: Real-Time Bitcoin Cost Identification to Improve Efficiency Using Lasso Regression in Comparison with Decision Tree
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Enhancing the Bitcoin cost prediction to improve accuracy using a decision tree in comparison with Lasso regression. For trend confirmations, we often utilize the financial phrases support and resistance to the prediction. Materials and Methods: The price of bitcoin is forecasted using a straightforward prediction technique called Lasso regression. The effectiveness of each model's performance on the task was evaluated, and the findings were examined. The goal of testing so many different models was to examine how the fundamental hypotheses of each of them varied. We used Lasso regression together with the best parameters to weigh the input variables because it is a reliable technique. Lasso regression is a Model based on a sample T-test with a value of p is 0.000 (Independent sample t-test <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p} < 0.05$</tex>). This indicates that there is a statistically significant difference between the two algorithms. The sample size calculation is done with a G-power pretest of 80%, threshold 0.05% and CI - 95%. Result: This research study indicated that using Novel Lasso Regression compared over Decision Tree with improved accuracy is 93.06% shows a better accuracy in the prediction of Bitcoin. Conclusion: Using Lasso regression compared over Decision Tree with improved accuracy.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Bayesian Neural Network for Robust Estimation of Signal Source Number in Acoustic Sensor Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In most of the signal source separation approaches, it is assumed that the number of signal sources is known, and hence, it cannot ensure satisfactory separation performance in real-world scenarios. The existing source counting methods lead to inaccurate estimation in the presence of noise, a limited number of samples, and the presence of outliers. Unlike other methods, this treatise formulates the problem in terms of supervised learning and obtained excellent performance even in challenging scenarios. The work introduced a Bayesian neural network to learn the eigenvalue pattern of the covariance matrix of the signals and achieve superior accuracy in source number separation tasks. The BNN discerns the intricate pattern in the data and accounts for the noise and uncertainties using a probabilistic framework, leading to noticeably higher efficacy. Besides, the lightweight BNN overcomes the predicament of overfitting and does not require a significant amount of data.

articleTitle: Designing a Meanderline-Based Ultraminiature Low-Profile Ultrawideband Antenna for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a customized ingestible and implantable antenna, utilizing a meanderline based design that has been specially engineered for wireless Ultra-wideband (UWB) endoscopy systems which can be used for different biomedical applications like microwave imaging, biomedical sensing and wireless power transfer (WPT) applications. The antenna exhibits a compact physical profile, measuring just 22×10×0.05 mm³. We investigate the performance of the capsule antenna within different organs of the digestive tract by employing a 3D human body voxel model in the CST Microwave Studio simulator. The omnidirectional radiation patterns exhibited by this design make it an ideal candidate for facilitating endoscopy communication. Notably, this antenna finds applications in a wide range of frequencies, including industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) at 868.0–868.8 MHz,0.915 GHz,2.45 GHz and 5.7 GHz, wireless medical telemetry services (WMTS) at 1.4 GHz and the UWB spectrum spanning from 3.1 to 10.6 GHz.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Tri-Band Microstrip Patch Antenna with an Optimized Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, we designed a rectangular triple-band microstrip patch antenna with a defective ground structure. The design is thoroughly discussed, and the results are simulated using ANSYS EDT. Our analysis is based on key elements like return loss, bandwidth, gain, and current distribution, providing a global assessment of the antenna's performance. In this proposed design, the first band exhibits a resonant frequency of 3.32 GHz with a bandwidth of 0.3 GHz and a return loss of -18.49 dB. The resonant frequency of the second band is 4.4 GHz, accompanied by a bandwidth of 0.09 GHz and a return loss of -15.57 dB. The third band operates at a resonant frequency of -5.54 GHz, offering a bandwidth of 0.26 GHz and a return loss of -14.6 dB. The proposed antenna exhibits various Wi-Max applications and wireless applications of STM32.

articleTitle: Compact Polarization-Insensitive FSS with Angularly Stability in Dual Stop-Band Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work, a compact, recurrence-specific frequency selective surface (FSS) with a super wide obstructing range is proposed which has relatively lower sensitivity to the incident polarization and proper angular stability. It comprises a perturbed square ring unit cell to obtain signal cancellation across a wide frequency range. The FSS of the recurrent type is composed of FR4 material that possesses a thickness measuring 1.6 mm. The proposed FSS shows the double band at 7.04 GHz and 16.05 GHz. The manipulation of the dimensions of the resonator allows for the adjustment of the desired total resonance and operational frequency range. This FSS design can be further extended to integrate with a reflector-type antenna for multi-band communication.

articleTitle: Intelligent Modeling of Circular Microstrip Antenna for RF Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper introduces the application of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) modeling to a circular microstrip patch antenna for RFEH applications. Two distinct ANN models are proposed for the forward and inverse modeling of the antenna. The forward model takes the geometrical parameters as inputs and produces the reflection coefficient as the output. In contrast, the inverse model, adopts a reverse approach. The models exhibit root mean square error of 0.0120 and 0.0126 for training and 0.0145 and 0.0131 for testing, respectively. These low error rates indicate the models' effectiveness in accurately predicting the antenna's behavior. To further evaluate the performance of the proposed models, a correlation coefficient statistical approach is employed. This analysis provides additional insights into the reliability and correlation between the predicted values and the actual performance of the antenna.

articleTitle: UHF Fractal Antenna for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A Compact UHF fractal antenna for space reentry vehicles and launch vehicles communication systems is proposed. The proposed fractal antenna design based on Peano space filling curves offers a size reduction of 80% compared to the normal rectangular microstrip patch antenna designed using same substrate at the same frequency. The overall dimensions of the realized Peano fractal antenna is 141mm x 141mm x 3mm. The proposed linearly polarized antenna is tuned to operate at 431.5MHz. This paper presents the design details of Peano fractal patch antenna and the performance comparison of different versions of the antenna in terms of S Parameter and gain. Antenna design is carried out in the presences of thermal protection system of the space re-entry vehicle.

articleTitle: Analyzing Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) for a Frequency-Reconfigurable Textenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This study thoroughly assesses a frequency-reconfigurable circularly polarized textenna crafted from jute material for on-body performance evaluation. This antenna achieves four distinct configurations by leveraging two BAR-64-03W pin diodes. In standalone conditions, In C1 mode it resonates at various frequencies of 2.4, 4.29, 5.78, and 9.39; in C2 it function at 5 and 5.9; in C3 it operates at 4.4 and 5.8 in C3; and in C4 it resonates at 3.5, 4.4, 5.3. CP occurs at frequencies of 2.4, 3.5, 5.8, and 5.9 GHz within these specified setups. SAR (Specific Absorption Rate) assessments were analysed for its performance near the human body to evaluate the antenna's effectiveness in close proximity. Using an HFSS software-based human phantom mimicking muscle, fat, and skin, SAR analysis was performed both with and without the antenna placed on the model. Impressively, the fabricated jute antenna exhibited excellent characteristics even when in contact with the human body. The correlation between the measurement and simulation was notably strong. SAR Inspection demonstrated the viability of this reconfigurable textenna for on-body communication applications, showcasing its effectiveness even at close proximity to human tissue.

Author Keywords: muscle fat and skin mimicking model

articleTitle: Multi-Channel Transmit-Receive Module (MCTRM) Operating In X-Band For Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The present paper relates a Multi-Channel Transmit-Receive Module (MCTRM) operating in X-Band for Radar applications. The MCTRM can include a plurality of independent Transmit-Receive Modules (TRM) which is operating on discrete power supplies, whereas MCTRM is realized on a single composite multi-layer PCB. The MCTRM can have a power splitter/combiner at transmit input/receive output. The MCTRM can include RF circuitry. The RF circuitry can be divided into four sections; Micro-strip based RF passive circuitry, common chain, transmits chain and receives chain. The manifold port connected is in-line with the RF transmission path whereas the antenna port connectors are perpendicular to the RF transmission path. Low Voltage Differential Signaling interface is used for communicating with the up-stream systems. For L VDS interface and to obtain fast switching between transmit and receive operation an FPGA-based control circuitry is used. All the active RF devices are pulsed using fast response Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor based logic. The timing of the pulsing circuitry along with the FPGA generated controls has been meticulously tuned to obtain a time difference of 150ns between transmit and receive operation. It is realized on a single composite multi-layer printed circuit board with blind vertical interconnects and is enclosed in a mechanical housing to achieve a compact form factor.

articleTitle: Investigation of Dispersion Control in Planar Rectangular Tape Helix Slow Wave Structure with Double-Positive Metamaterial Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents, a modified dispersion characteristics of rectangular tape helix (RTH) slow wave structure (SWS) by using double-positive (DPS) metamaterial (MTM) loading for wideband applications. The limited operation bandwidth associated with the conventional RTH restricts the applications for wideband frequency range. Therefore, the DPS-MTM comprising an array of sub-wavelength square split-ring resonators (SSRR) is thoroughly investigated. A full wave simulation is performed to extract the effective material parameters and DPS-MTM is systematically loaded on the opposite faces of dielectric support rods of the RTH. The post integration of DPS-MTM offers a flat-to-slightly negative dispersion characteristics in forward-wave mode with simulated normalized phase velocity (averaged) of 5% over the entire bandwidth (1–10 GHz). The flat band range of the phase velocity curve exceeds 70% in the desired region (±5% margin), by varying number of Unit Cells (UCs). Hence, the proposed structure attains the intended flat dispersion along with high interaction impedance of SWS rendering it suitable for the wideband operation of traveling wave tube (TWT) amplifier.

articleTitle: An Open Book Shaped 3-D Patch Antenna Design for C Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Microstrip patch antennas are popular because of their small size, low cost, and ease of manufacturing. They are used in many different applications. Nonetheless, the antenna designer faces a constant challenge from the market's desire for new technologies that offer high performance and compactness. The limitations of traditional techniques for increasing bandwidth and gain are primarily related to their difficult implementation or poor radiation performance. This paper presents a novel patch antenna layout that takes advantage of the customizable form factor. It is simple, yet effective. A suitable alteration to the radiator's vertical profile is implemented. The designed antenna used for C band applications is resonating at 6.54GHz, 8.1GHz, having the maximum gain at 7.4dBi. To achieve dual resonance and an improved gain, a partially reflective surface with a cavity resonator is introduced, and an open book shape has been chosen as a demonstration of idea without sacrificing generality. The suggested method enables a normal flat microstrip patch's bandwidth to be increased from 4% to 7%.

articleTitle: LTCC Antenna for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper a meander line antenna based on LTCC technology is proposed for WLAN applications. the antenna design consists of 3 layers developed on high permittivity ceramic chip of size 9×2×1mm3 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon \mathrm{r} = 30$ </tex>. the study includes the effect on antenna performance due to different types of ground planes, location of antenna on ground plane. the results shows that the antenna characteristics like frequency, return loss, far field gain are significantly effect by the ground plane.

articleTitle: Integrating Gas-Sensitive Layers on Rectangular Patch Antenna for Enhanced Gas Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The study explores Melanine, Zinc oxide (ZNO) and Ferric Oxide (Fe2O3) are the materials significant for their ability of sensing various gases. The Organic materials and polymers with the structure of melanine supports gas detection. However, Fe2O3 & ZNO are named for their ability of gas detection. When they are exposed to certain gases their surface conductivity changes making them suitable for gas detection. In the current investigation when the patch antenna is coated with Melanine, Zinc oxide and Ferric Oxide with thickness of 5 micrometers, these materials are strategically employed for the detection of gases, with a focus on observing changes in resonating frequencies of 2.4 GHz resembling the indication of gas presence. The investigation aims to enhance the sensitivity and specificity of gas detection in various applications.

articleTitle: Three-Way, Equal-Phase High Power Divider & Combiner with a Novel method of improving Isolation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The present paper relates to design and realization of microwave power dividers, combiners. A three way high power divider and high power three way combiner with dual directional coupler are presented. This invention is a novel method of implementation of three way high power divider and combiner using modified Wilkinson concept and by adding circulator in each arm after the distributed quarter wave microstrip line which avoids high power resistor across ports & improves isolation performance over wider bandwidth. Also in each arm of divider, a high power attenuator is used for amplitude balancing between ports. In-phase power combiner/divider is a common circuit employed in many microwave systems in Defence applications like SDR, Radar & EW systems.

articleTitle: X-band Waveform Generator with Calibration feature for Active Phased Array Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper describes the architecture of Waveform Generator along with calibration feature for X-Band Active Phased Array Radar application. It is based on a hybrid synthesizer architecture using Direct Digital Synthesizer (DDS) and Phase Locked Loop (PLL). Module generates Linear Frequency Modulated X-Band frequency during transmit mode and IF (Intermediate Frequency) offseted X-Band spot frequency during receive mode which minimize the hardware requirement. It also has a phase calibration feature for Radar transmit and receive chain. Along with the waveform generation this module is also generating the timing and controls required for the entire Radar sub modules. It is realized on a single multilayer PCB without any degradation in performance.

articleTitle: Implementation of Serial FPDP and 10G Ethernet in an FPGA Based Real Time Embedded Hardware
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Today's radar technology demands the use of huge aperture antenna arrays for detection and tracking of targets from a range of hundreds of kilometers. This results in a complex RF manifold where a large number of RF channels in parallel are provided as input to the radar receiver. Subsequently, these inputs are digitized and forwarded to a real time embedded hardware for further processing. Since the number of RF channels are quite high and reception as well as analysis of the incoming data have to be completed for a particular dwell within a matter of few milliseconds, therefore we require high speed serial interfaces from receiver to receive the data and process it in shortest time. Moreover, a copy of the raw data is also required to be forwarded to the signal processor over 10G Ethernet interface. In this paper, we highlight such a design and implementation of a serial Front Panel Data Port (FPDP) interface working at 2.5 Gbaud/lane and a number of such lanes are processed successfully in parallel. Next, we present the design and implementation of the 10G Ethernet interface along with the validation of data integrity at the destination.

articleTitle: Design of Circular Microstrip Antenna with Metasurface Superstate for Wifi Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Metasurfaces are sub wavelength thick counterparts of two-dimensional (2D) or Planar metamaterials. They are broadly investigated and implemented in electromagnetic applications due to their light weight and ease of fabrication. This Article began with the motive of developing Circular Microstrip patch antennas and then it moved to developing and employment of metasurface superstate on top of the Circular patch antennas. After putting a superstate on the patch antennas, the characteristics of the antenna like Gain, VSWR and Return loss are observed to improve for Metasurface superstate. This Article mainly focused on improving the gain of the antennas and on average of 1 dB gain is observed to increase after putting the superstate. The Metasurface Superstate Antennas are fabricated function at frequencies of 2.4GHz and 5.2 GHz and implemented on FR-4 Material. The proposed Metasurface Antenna is primarily used as a router in retail, service provider & Wi-Fi 5 GHz UNII (Unlicensed National Information Infrastructure).

articleTitle: Cross Slotted Antenna at X Band for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The most widely used patch antennas in wireless communication systems are microstrip ones. Because of constraints on payload, the antennas on board should be compact and less in weight. One of the key parts of a wireless communication system is the antenna. The paper suggests the design of a star slotted antenna model operates at a resonating X band frequency of 11.26 GHz and a return loss of - 47.56 dB is observed over a wide bandwidth of 212MHz and a Gain of 4.1 dB. The design aims that a rectangular microstrip antenna is proposed with tiny and narrow cross shaped slots on radiating patch antenna. The antenna has star-shaped slots at the patch's corners, and one slot in the middle of the patch has twice the size of the corner star slot on a radiating element to achieve wide bandwidth. HFSS software was used for the purpose of optimum design and simulation. The outcome has been demonstrated by the proposed model's performance with radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Sierpinski Gasket Fractal-Based Microwave Metamaterial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a Sierpinski fractal-based Microwave Metamaterial Absorber (MMA). Sierpinski fractal is a self-repetitive structure which can provide a dual-band operation. In the designed geometry, the sierpinski triangle having dual-band performance at X and K bands. In this study, a sierpinski fractal has been designed up to it's third iteration and analysed for return loss. The sierpinski triangle is designed upon a FR-4 substrate which is having a thickness of 0.8mm. The SGMMA_1 has its dual-band operation at 8.2GHz and 20.24GHz with peak absorption of 98.3% and 91.9%. SGMMA_2 shows its dual-band operation at 8.1GHz and 20GHz with peak absorption of 97.5% and 96.2%. SGMMA_3 has its dual-band operation at 8.4GHz and 20.65GHz showing peak absorption at 97.5% and 96.5%. Furtherly, the structure is very well investigated for its surface current distribution. This proposed MMA especially used in applications of warfare and in microwave sensors that are used in environmental monitoring.

articleTitle: Current Trends of Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Microwave imaging is a non-invasive technique that uses microwaves (usually in the range of 0.1 to 100 GHz) to create images of objects or materials. The technique is based on the fact that microwaves are absorbed, reflected, or transmitted differently by different materials, depending on their electrical and dielectric properties. By measuring these interactions, it is possible to create images of the internal structure of an object or material. Proposed work is focus on the recent trends and applications. Microwave imaging has several advantages over other imaging techniques, such as X-ray or ultrasound. It is non-ionizing, which means it does not produce harmful ionizing radiation. It is also relatively inexpensive and can be used to image a wide range of materials, including biological tissues, structural materials, and industrial materials. Applications of microwave imaging include medical imaging, industrial inspection, and non-destructive testing (NDT). In medical imaging, microwave imaging can be used to image the human body for diagnostic purposes. In industrial inspection, it can be used to inspect materials and structures for defects or abnormalities. In NDT, it is used to evaluate the integrity of materials and structures without damaging them.

articleTitle: Simplified Biasing AFSS Microwave Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized active frequency selective surface (AFSS) based microwave absorber designed to operate in 3.4-10.56 GHz operating band. This response has been obtained with the 0.088λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>total thickness where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>is the wavelength corresponding to the lowest -10dB operating frequency. The dual polarization has been achieved by cascading the unit cells, and it elevates the need for metallic vias to supply the biasing voltage to the NXP #BAP70-03 p-i-n diodes. The structure also shows the deep reflectance at various frequencies, which is useful in achieving a very high degree of absorption over the wide frequency band. The complete structure, its biasing arrangements, and measured results will be presented during the conference.

articleTitle: Linearly Polarised Normal Mode Helix Antenna at UHF-Band for Inter-Satellite Communication Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a light weight, linearly polarized normal mode helix antenna for inter-satellite communication application in UHF band is discussed. Near isotropic radiation pattern except along the boresight axis makes it suitable for inter satellite communication at shorter distances consuming low power. It has return loss better than 15dB and minimum coverage gain of -5dBi over ±50° with respect to axis perpendicular to boresight axis.

articleTitle: Intelligent Torque Control System for Vehicle Safety: A Human-Centric Approach with ESP8266 and Blink IoT Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper introduces an intelligent torque control system designed for heightened vehicle safety by adapting torque output based on passenger types. Prioritizing the safety of children and the elderly with torque limits of 40, and accommodating adults with a limit of 70, the system operates without torque limits in emergencies for swift responses. Core components include the ESP8266 microcontroller, LM 398N motor driver, four geared motors, Blink IoT module [2], battery, and TP 4056 charging module, working seamlessly for optimal performance. User-friendly features include three buttons - Child, Adult, and Emergency - enabling easy torque setting selection. The research contributes significantly to vehicle safety systems by introducing a flexible torque control mechanism, aiming to reduce accident risks and enhance overall road passenger safety. The integration of IoT technology and intelligent torque control holds promising implications for the future of automotive safety. Key components highlighted include the ESP8266 microcontroller [1], LM 398N, four geared motors, Blink IoT module, battery, and TP 4056.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of SIW Cavity Filter for 14.5 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel miniaturization technique for the SIW Cavity Filter, enabling its operation below the fundamental frequency while minimizing changes to its physical dimensions. The filter has been designed at 14.5GHz frequency with the help of Ansys HFSS and MATLAB RFPCB Toolbox ™ . The technique involves the incorporation of additional stubs at the filter's edges, along with the removal of C-shaped cavities from the patch. The study explores two configurations, vertical and horizontal, providing comprehensive illustrations of the technique's efficacy. Key advantages of this approach include the ability to electronically tune the fundamental frequency and seamless integration with a wide range of devices.

articleTitle: A Study of Wire Bi-Conical Antenna for Wide-Band Application in Radio Astronomy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, we describe the characteristics of biconical antennas that can be used in wide-band radio astronomy applications. While the theory of a biconical antenna has been established, the effect of cone angle with a discretized cone (wired biconical antenna) is still unknown. As part of this study, different numbers of wires and cone angles are used in creating biconical antennas. Our study examines twelve combinations of 4, 8, and 12, one metre wired biconical antenna structures with cone angles of 30°, 45°, 60°, and 75°. These biconical antenna configurations were simulated using CST Suite software, with a frequency range of 100 MHz to 3 GHz. It is observed that the bandwidth of operation depends on both the number of wires and the cone angle, wherein the cone angles directly affects operational bandwidth, gain and the radiation pattern of the antenna. Moreover, changing the cone angle can also result in a multi-beam pattern as well as antenna gain up to 6.4 dBi.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Gain of Wireless Power Transmission System Using Negative Index Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a negative index metamaterial (NIMTM) superstrate is proposed to enhance the transmission capacity of the Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) System. This WPT system is useful in charging the battery of biomedical implants. A double-sided circular split ring unit structure is used to achieve the negative index property of the metamaterial(MTM). Here the metamaterial superstrate enhances the received signal level at the implant by acting as a lens and focusing the electromagnetic waves from the transmitting source to the receiving implant. This system operates in the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band. The simulation results are presented and an increase in the gain of 1.3dB (from 8dB to 9.3dB) is observed on the transmitting side of this WPT system by the introduction of metamaterial.

articleTitle: Towards Multi-Sensing Aspects: Robust Passive Chipless RFID Sensor Tag
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The work presents a passive battery-less chipless RFID tag for multi-sensing parameters. The tag designed for 1-bit data encoding, has been examined for humidity as well as temperature sensing simultaneously. The humidity sensing tag has been designed using Kapton HN substrate, along with copper electrode. The operational frequency of sensor tag is 11.25 GHz and temperature sensitive tag is 5.5 GHz. For monitoring temperature fluctuations in atmosphere, Rogers RT/Duroid 6010.2LM has been acquired as temperature sensitive substrate. To analyze the selectivity and sensitivity of temperature sensor tag, the slot of tag is coated with Kapton heat resistant sheet. Through simulations, it has been analyzed that the tag temperature sensing response is not affected by humidity variations in environment. The work is capable of being utilized for smart wireless sensor networks in industrial internet-of-things (IIoT).

articleTitle: A Rugged Synchronization Scheme for Large Aperture Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Large Aperture Antenna Arrays are increasingly becoming important. This is primarily because of the need to transmit high power of the order of hundreds of kilowatts. This necessitates the usage of thousands of Transmit Receive Modules (TRMs) which are in turn controlled by hundreds of Digital LRUs arranged in a series parallel configuration across multiple levels of hierarchy. This arrangement calls for a rugged synchronization scheme to be implemented in the antenna so that it can be ascertained that all the TRMs at the lowermost level in the hierarchy play the same forward dwell which is transmitted from the Master Timing Generator Module. Existing trigger-based synchronization schemes or carrying separate clock lines across each level of the hierarchy is ruled out in this case because of the small size of the modules which in turn, restricts the number of I/O lines which are carried across each level of hierarchy. Synchronization is also required for the antenna to handshake with other sub-systems of the radar. This paper discusses such novel and rugged synchronization schemes with minimum hardware complexity which were designed, implemented, tested and successfully field proven.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Band SIW Cavity Backed Ring Slot Antenna for X/Ka-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work discusses about a design of a dual-band aperture-sharing cavity-backed slot antenna operating at X/Ka band applications. A microstrip line-fed square patch antenna area is redesigned with a coaxial-fed circular model substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity structure. The square patch antenna design is intended to operate at X-band with a 5.5 dBi gain, and SIW circular cavity-backed annular ring slot design is intended to operate at Ka-band with a gain of 7.7 dBi. This dual-band antenna achieves satisfactory isolation of 30 dB between two ports. The proposed design has an application of remote sensing and fifth-generation (5G).

articleTitle: Improving Secrecy Rate in NOMA Network with Jamming Schmes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This article explores the issue of physical layer security (PLS) through an analysis of a Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) network using multiple jamming strategies. In this network, a source transmits multiplexed signals to NOMA users when Eve is present. A jammer node adds interference signals to prevent Eve from wiretapping the secret information of the NOMA users. By deploying a new control-jammer (CJ) strategy to this network, it is possible to maximize secrecy rate at both NOMA users while working under a total power constraint. The main focus of the proposed work is on evaluating the PLS analysis of the network in terms of secrecy rate, with particular attention to the CJ condition. Additionally, the study measures the security performance difference between CJ and other jamming methods. Notably, the simulation findings confirm that CJ is effective in boosting the security of the NOMA network compared with other jamming strategies.

articleTitle: Semi-Lumped Cross-Coupled Non-reciprocal Bandpass Filter for 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper is based on a design and characterization of a fourth-order semi-lumped cross-coupled band pass filter implementing non-reciprocity at the mid band frequency of 1 GHz using spatio-temporal modulation applied on resonators. This work methodically combines static and time-modulators resonators using direct coupled lumped elements with an additional source-load cross-coupled structure. The former generates the non-reciprocal response while the latter manifests a highly selective passband. The concept is first of its kind and the simulated non-reciprocal filtering isolation response show enhanced skirt frequency characteristics in addition to a moderately high reverse isolation within the passband in the backward direction. The insertion loss, return loss, and isolation achieved are 3.4 dB, >15 dB, and >13 dB, respectively. This non-reciprocal filter configuration can be equipped in 5G FR1 bands owing to the highly selective response.

articleTitle: A Wideband Single Polarization Antenna for Precision Cosmology in S-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper we present a prototype antenna design for the Array of Precision Spectrometers for the Epoch of RecombinAtion(APSERa), a future ground-based radio array with a primary science goal of detecting faint spectral distortions in the Cosmic Microwave Background. The printed planar monopole antenna backed by a square metallic reflector operates over 2.7 to 4 GHz. It is designed to be nominally achromatic and easy to fabricate in large numbers to form an array of over 100 identical antennas. The antenna presented herein has nominal maximum gain towards the zenith, wide half power beam widths (HPBW) of mean value~ 56° in E-plane and ~ 113° in H-plane and a smooth return-loss with just one inflection. These are all desirable characteristics for APSERa. The antenna was designed and optimized in CST microwave studio. The antenna structure is fabricated and characterized in anechoic chamber. The measured antenna properties are compared with simulation results. We conclude with discussions on suitability of the designed antenna for APSERa and suggest improvements toward the same.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Metamaterial Absorbers for C- and X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work proposes a broadband metamaterial absorber. It is made up of three layers: metal, FR4 and metal. The simulation outcomes indicate both broad-spectrum and maximum absorption peaks from 4.71 GHz to 8.1 GHz, and the absorption rates are 90% to 100%, respectively. The influence of structural elements is analysed and optimized. The examination involves analyzing the electric field and surface current patterns when subjected to normally incident transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) waves. The simulation outcomes demonstrate that it exhibits insensitivity to polarization, possesses a straightforward structure, boasts a high absorption rate, features a broad bandwidth, and finds application in various fields such as electromagnetic camouflage, bolometers, sensors, and more.

articleTitle: Direction Finding by Time Modulated Linear Antenna Arrays Using Root-MUSIC Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a study on direction finding using Time Modulated Antenna array with Root-MUSIC algorithm for multiple non-coherent sources in the presence of white gaussian noise. Root-MUSIC algorithm is found to reduce the computational complexity and increase the speed with good accuracy. The performance of the proposed algorithm for parameters such as the number of elements, inter element spacing, incident angle and SNR is studied. The proposed algorithm shows better performance compared to MUSIC and power spectrum estimation method except at low SNR. The numerical simulations are carried out in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of OFDM, FBMC and UFMC for Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents the comparison of 5G modulation algorithms such as Filter Band Multi Carrier (FBMC) and Universal Filter Multi Carrier (UFMC) to Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) are proposed, which is utilized in 4G communications. We evaluate critical characteristics of various modulation methods to assess each technique's advantage in 5G wireless communication. For assessment and evaluation, the metrics Power Spectral Density (PSD), Bit Error Rate (BER), Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) and Peak to Average Power Ratio (PAPR) are considered.

articleTitle: An Efficient Dual-Band Rectifier for GSM/Wi-Fi Bands Operated Microwave Power Transfer Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Microwave power transmission (MPT) is a popular technique to provide wake-up power to any low-power devices located at remote locations. A rectenna circuit is therefore needed to capture the RF signal from the surroundings and convert it to electrical DC. This DC power can be utilized to feed the low-power sensors. For efficient performance of rectenna circuits, an efficient rectifier is required. For this purpose, a dual-band rectifier operating at GSM1.8 and WiFi/WLAN2.45 GHz is proposed in this paper. A single diode in series topology and a dual-band matching network have been utilized for RF to DC rectification. The rectifier achieved RF to DC power conversion efficiency (RF-DC PCE) of 61.4% and 54.9% at 1.8, and 2.45 GHz, respectively at 0 dBm. At -30 dBm rectifier has RF-DC PCE of 1.87% and 1.2% at 1.8 and 2.45 GHz respectively. Also, the RF-DC PCE of the rectifier exceeds 50% for the two bands 1.71-1.92 GHz and 2.26-2.52 GHz at 0 dBm.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Parasitically Coupled DRA using Parametric Analysis for High Gain Using Aperture Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A dielectric resonator is indeed a piece of dielectric material, often made of ceramics or other suitable materials, that is used as a resonator for microwave frequency bands. The dielectric resonator provides higher efficiency, absence of surface waves and are also compatible. The antenna consists of one input feed line and five rectangular dielectric resonator units, and the power is coupled to these units through aperture coupling using novel microstrip lines. The gap between each dielectric resonators 4.75mm for getting the high bandwidth and gain. We are using the aperture coupling feeding technique in the antenna. Aperture-coupled fed DRAs offer key advantages like Integration with MMICs, lower ohmic losses, improved isolation from the feed network. MMICs or Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuits, are essential semiconductor components in microwave technology. These comp act circuits perform crucial tasks like signal amplification, processing, and beamforming. Parasitically coupled DRAs optimize performance by utilizing nearby parasitic elements without direct electrical links. Strategic adjustments in parasitic element position and size tailor radiation patterns, impedance and gain.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation Two Element MIMO Antenna of Metamaterial Based Superstrate for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This study looks at a two-element, meta material-loaded MIMO antenna with frequencies of 2.4 GHz and 5.1 GHz, respectively. Maximal gain and directivity are what we aim to achieve by positioning two elements in different orientations, such as0°, orthogonal 90°, and 180°. Then figure out the MIMO antenna's ECC and MEG. We employed a hybrid Meta surface split beam antenna in this piece. Multi-beam antennas with excellent directivity are required for the 5G mobile network. Multi-beam antennas with excellent directivity are required for the 5G mobile network. To achieve it, you can use an array antenna. Using a low frequency antenna increases the overall network's complexity and scalability. In order to direct surface current, a Meta surface (MS) with high gain and multi-beam characteristics is suggested. A square split ring resonator (SSRR) and a U-shaped unit cell Meta surface are employed as the superstrate to each rectangular patch antenna. By controlling this coupled Meta surface design, it is possible to segregate the radiation by generating opposing current flows on the unit cell. The hybrid Meta surface superstrate and antenna are built on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$FR-4(r=4.4)$</tex>. The HFSS program was used to simulate the antenna.

articleTitle: Self-Isolated Frequency Reconfigurable two-port MIMO Antenna for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work two-port multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna with self-isolation between antenna elements is presented. Initially, the proposed antenna is constructed as a single-port square-shaped radiating patch connected diagonally with a stub to operate the antenna in frequency reconfigurable mode. A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2}\times\mathbf{2}$</tex> mm slot is cut at the middle part of the stub for implementing reconfigurability on the radiating patch to operate the antenna in multi-functional mode. Later the proposed antenna is converted to two-port frequency reconfigurable MIMO antenna that realizes an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}_{11}$</tex> below -10 dB intended for two resonant bands operating at 3.79 GHz (3.41-4.04 GHz) with pin-diode off-mode and 4.53 GHz (4.69-4.88 GHz) in on-mode with maximum peak realized gain of 4.93 dB at diode off-mode and 4.55 dB in pin diode on-mode. moreover, the gain is enhanced by 1.5 dB after converting to the two-port antenna. The two feeding ports of the proposed antenna are positioned orthogonal to each other to permit the antenna in self-isolation mode without connecting any de-coupling circuit and maintaining the mutual coupling <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{S}_{21})$</tex> below-21 dB in off-mode and -29.50 dB in diode on-mode. The distance between antenna elements is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.12 \ {\lambda}0$</tex>. In addition to that, two-port MIMO of envelope correlation coefficient (ECC), channel capacity loss (CCL), total active reflection coefficient (TARC), mean effective gain (MEG), and diversity gain (DG) are simulated. The designed antenna is applicable for 5G new radio (NR) bands of n48, n78 in off-mode, and n79 in on-mode respectively.

articleTitle: Effect of DGS on Slotted Square Patch Antenna for 5G and LTE Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper introduces a square patch antenna designed for 5G and LTE network applications, featuring pentagon and hexagon slots at the center of the square patch. The dimensions of the proposed antenna are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$37\times 34\times 1.6\ \text{mm}^{3}$</tex> and the dimensions of the patch are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$17\times 17\ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. The proposed antenna resonates at 3.95GHz with a bandwidth of 120MHz (3.88GHz to 4GHz) with a peak gain of 5dBi. Incorporating DGS results in an improvement of bandwidth to 2.08GHz and gain to 5.4dBi, with a resonating frequency at 4.15 GHz. This antenna operates in S and C bands. Simulations are carried out using Ansys HFSS software.

articleTitle: Isolation Enhancement in Fractral Inspired MIMO Antenna Using DGS for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this study, we present a design aimed at enhancing the isolation among elements of a fractal inspired antenna. We explore and introduce a single-band multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna of the fractal inspired geometry, specifically designed to operate in the frequency range of 2.58 to 4.03GHz. To enhance the isolation between the elements, we effectively utilize a Defected Ground Structure (DGS). The overall dimensions of the proposed antenna are 38mm×40mm×1.6mm. By incorporating the DGS, we achieve an isolation level as low as -51.7dB at 3.3GHz between antennas. The designed DGS is customized to reduce mutual coupling among closely spaced antenna elements while maintaining radiation performance, compact size and a low envelope correlation coefficient.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of SIW Cavity Backed Slot Antenna Using High-Order Radiation Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this study, we investigate bandwidth enhancement in a Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed slot antenna through high-order radiation modes. The design features an SIW cavity resonator with a precisely etched rectangular radiating slot on the top layer. A folded grounded coplanar waveguide feeding system achieves impedance matching for three higher-order modes, each below −10 dB within a shared frequency band. This matching significantly contributes to the overall bandwidth improvement. The optimized antenna exhibits an impressive 1.428 GHz impedance bandwidth, covering 10.197 GHz to 11.625 GHz. The operational bandwidth displays three distinct resonance dips at 10.23 GHz, 10.906 GHz, and 11.325 GHz, with corresponding gain values of 8.116 dBi, 9.224 dBi, and 8.023 dBi. The proposed design boasts advantages like a simple single-layer structure, wideband capability, and high gain, making it suitable for integration into X-band communication systems.

articleTitle: Horn Feed Assembly Modification for INCUS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: INCUS (INvestigation of Convective UpdraftS) is an Earth Science project approved by NASA in 2022. The goal of the mission is to study in detail how water vapor and droplets move inside tropical storms and thunderstorms and understand their effects on weather and climate models. To carry out this study, the mission will use three almost identical SmallSats, each one equipped with a Ka-band radar heritage of Raincube. The deployable mesh reflector antenna is a new 1.6 m design provided by Tendeg. This paper presents the general architecture of the three observatories with particular emphasis on the radar antenna subsystem design. In particular, the design and fabrication of the feed assembly will be presented along with measured and calculated RF performance parameters. Modified horn designs based on the measurement observations will also be presented.

articleTitle: Data Visualization of Weather Conditions in Hilly Regions using Wireless Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Applications as diverse as home automation and agriculture depend on weather monitoring. The design and deployment of a low-cost weather station that uses IoT technology to gather, transmit, and visualize local weather information are presented in this work. The system is built around an ESP8266 microprocessor and includes a DHT11 sensor for measuring temperature and humidity, a rain sensor for spotting precipitation, and an LDR sensor for keeping track of light levels. The weather station's findings show that it can deliver precise and current information on temperature, humidity, the likelihood of rain, and light intensity. In this paper, difficulties as well as potential future advancements are explored. For individuals and groups interested in keeping track of local weather conditions, the offered weather station offers an adaptable and practical solution. It is suitable for a variety of applications, from home weather monitoring to educational projects.

articleTitle: A Broadband Rectifier with High Power Conversion Efficiency and High Power Handling Capability for Microwave Power Transfer Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Microwave power transfer (MPT) is the technique to transfer radio-frequency (RF) energy from one place to another place without using wire in the form of microwave signals. At the receiver end, an antenna circuit is needed to receive the signal. A circuit known as a rectifier is also needed to convert this received microwave energy into DC energy to store. The conversion takes place using a nonlinear rectifying device called a Schottky diode. In this work, a broadband rectifier with a high power conversion efficiency and high-power handling capability is reported. For this purpose, a Schottky diode having a 15V breakdown voltage has been chosen. The rectifier covers the GSM 1.8, LTE 2.1, and Wi-Fi 2.45 GHz bands. The rectifier has a sensitivity of -10 dBm and has power conversion efficiency (PCE) greater than 65% from 1.73 to 2.65 GHz at a 20 dBm input power level. The PCE exceeds 60% from 1.645 to 2.54 GHz at 13 dBm. The maximum PCE reached 78.4% at 2.47 GHz at 20 dBm input power.

articleTitle: Effect of Realistic Behavior of High- Frequency Antennas in Spectral Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In the evolving era of wireless communication systems, the significance of antenna noise and its profound influence on the antenna signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and the overall communication SNR cannot be overstated. This paper delves into an exploration of antenna noise, antenna SNR, and the quality of wireless communication systems. The study begins by elucidating the fundamental principles of antenna Noise, encompassing both internal and external noise within the antenna system. Reviewing existing literature, the paper unveils the diverse factors contributing to antenna noise, ranging from environmental conditions to electronic components. These factors are termed as mismatch loss and radiation efficiency of the antenna. Furthermore, the paper meticulously analyzes the antenna SNR as a bridge connecting antenna noise to the communication quality. The antenna noise and factors also affect the SNR and spectral efficiency in the communication system having large-scale fading (Path loss).

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Metasurface-BasedHybrid Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A metasurface-based Hybrid CylindricalDielectric Resonator Antenna (HC-DRA)is proposed for getting circularlypolarized radiation at 5 GHz wireless applications. The proposed antenna contains a cylindrical DRA, amodified minkowski based metasurface, and a coaxial probe. The proposed structure improves the bandwidth and gain of thecylindrical DRA. The metasurfaceact as a reflector and the antenna radiations is confined to the surface of the dielectric resonator. In this design, a DRA is placed over the metasurfaceand by adjusting the metasurface's dimensions, the radiated field's polarization can be controlled,Which acts as a superstrate. The metasurface consistsof an array of unequal rectangular-shaped unit cells that exhibit a wideband 3-dB axialratio bandwidth of 570Hz (4.72 GHz-5.29 GHz). A6.87 dBirealized gain is obtained across the frequency range from 4.27 GHz to 5.77 GHz with a center frequency of 5GHz.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Band Modified Cylindrical-DRA Based MIMO Antenna for WLAN / X-Band Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A novel modified cylindrical dielectric resonator-based MIMO antenna is presented for WLAN and X-band applications. On the above Rogers substrate (RT / duroid 5880), alumina or ceramics-based two-element dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) are positioned in opposition. The microstrip line excites each element and resonates in a dual-band, one band at 5.05 - 5.86 GHz and the other wideband at 8.04 - 11.38 GHz. Isolation is improved (≤ -15 dB ) by rotating the feeding line of each element at an angle of 180° opposite feed between C-DRA without any decoupling structure. The proposed MIMO antenna performance parameters like bandwidth, efficiency, gain, and isolation are investigated. Further, MIMO antenna metrics are carried out.

articleTitle: Design of Class-F Power Amplifier for Active Antennas Operating over the UWB regime
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A Class F Power Amplifier operating at 10 GHz frequency is presented here for overall improvement of radiated power for 5G/6G communications. The designed power amplifier (PA) consists of gate and drain biasing networks, input and output matching networks and harmonic tuning network. An Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) high-efficiency class-F power amplifier is designed based on the proposed method. A high voltage gallium nitride (GaN) high electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) on a Silicon Carbide substrate is used. A peak drain efficiency of 70.5 % for class-F amplifier is measured at 10 GHz frequency. The class-F amplifier achieves a peak effective radiated power of 39 dBm, and power added efficiency (PAE) is over 50 %.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Square Fractal Shaped Planar Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents the design, analysis and simulation of microstrip patch antenna in the field of wireless communication networks. This antenna is used for the design optimization of a microstrip patch antenna tuned over a frequency range of 14 GHz with a return loss of -19dB. The gain over this microstrip patch antenna is over a range of 9dB. This paper mainly focuses on how the analysis and development of a square fractal-shaped planar antenna is done. This research provides the feasibility and advantages of how the fractal-shaped geometries in planar antennae is enhanced for wireless communication systems..

articleTitle: Area Efficient Sparse-4 Diminished-1 Modulo 2n + 1 Adder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A modulo adder is a very important component for implementing arithmetic computations in Residue Number System (RNS). The RNS is used in RESIDUE arithmetic, and in digital signal processing applications. Mainly, the modulo <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{\mathrm{n}}+1$</tex> adder has great applicability in RNS implementations for several applications. This paper designed an area-efficient sparse-4-diminished-1 modulo <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{\mathrm{n}}+1$</tex> adder with a modified carry select block. The proposed carry select block uses the Binary to Excess one Converter (BEC) to reduce area. The modified diminished-1 modulo <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{\mathrm{n}}+1$</tex> adder architecture reduces the area without an increase in delay, leading to better performance. Based on this modification, we simulated the 4,8,16,32-bit modified diminished-1 modulo <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{\mathrm{n}}+1$</tex> adder architectures in the Xilinx ISE simulator, and synthesized them in a cadence 180 nm standard cell library, and compared them with the existing methods. This work exhibits a 3.8% area and 1 % delay reduction with a 2.1 % power overhead.

articleTitle: Study of False Alarm Using Sliding Window for Pulse Detection Radar System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Efficient spectrum sensing is essential to modern radar systems in order to maximize the utilization of available frequency bands, guarantee interference abatement, and improve overall system performance. In this paper, we will be discussing a new technique for detecting signal frequencies in radar bands using a sliding window method. The suggested approach seeks to detect and identify any interference or signal anomalies in a dynamic radar environment by taking advantage of the intrinsic time-frequency features of radar signals. By dividing the received radar signal into overlapping parts, the sliding window approach makes it possible to continuously monitor the spectral content. Different signal processing and detection methods can be used inside each window to determine whether signals of interest, like radar targets or possible sources of interference, are present. This method's main advantages are its flexibility in responding to shifting signal conditions, its real-time monitoring capabilities, and its capacity to discriminate between main radar signals and other interfering signals. It also offers an analysis tool for the radar environment's spectral and temporal properties. Experiments and simulation results are used to illustrate the concept and show how well it works for identifying and describing signals in radar bands. Additionally, this sliding window-based spectrum sensing technique is adaptable and can be used with a range of radar systems, which enhances radar spectrum management and guarantees the dependability and resilience of radar operations.

articleTitle: A 28 GHz FSS Backed SIW Slotted Array Antenna with Ultra Reduced Sidelobes for Ground Surveillance & RADAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: At Ka Band, a Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) based <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \times 8$</tex> Slotted Array Antenna has been designed and simulated in which ultra sidelobe reduction has been performed by means of nonuniform distribution of offset slot distances obeying Gauss or Normal Distribution Equation. Further a FSS is designed beneath the proposed antenna as a reflector for diminution of the generated and undesired back lobe while directing its radiation towards the main lobe. Further multiple number of the designed antenna model is arranged specially so as to get a radiation pattern of an isotropic antenna with high gain all around 360° angle. A parametric study is also performed on the center-to-center distance of separation of the models & some observations along with formulation has also been done so as to minimize the mutual coupling among them and obtain an optimum value for maximum radiation angle out of 360° with gain above half power.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Wide-Band Modified CPW-Fed Bow Tie Radial Slot Antenna with Rectangular Stubs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A wide-band dual-band antenna for WLAN applications is proposed in this paper. This work illustrates the impact of stubs on bow-tie CPW-Fed antennas. The design gives dual-band performance, achieving a wide band at 2.45 GHz and 5.65 GHz. The configuration of the antenna design with a thickness of 1 mm and an area of 69mm x 45mm. Compared to conventional slot antenna, the radiation bandwidth surged to give 1.62 GHz bandwidth at 2.4 GHz, making it a good candidate for WLAN applications.

articleTitle: A Tri-Band Shared Aperture Binomial Antenna Array AIR-SAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: An article explores the concept of a shared aperture antenna utilizing a three-band (C/X/Ku) binomial antenna array with linear polarization. The ingenuity lies in coupling three distinct bands within the same aperture, each resonating at different frequencies. Binomial arrays are chosen for their compactness, low polarization, high isolation, and dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$210\times 60\times 0.8\ \text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. The CST Microwave Studio Simulator is employed to yield results. At the operating frequencies of 5.3 GHz, 9.3 GHz, and 13.265 GHz, the isolation between port-1 and port-2 is −48 dB, between port-1 and port-3 is −58 dB, and between port-2 and port-3 is −57 dB. For the C-band, X-band, and Ku-band, the bandwidth is measured at 0.032%, with a return loss of −15.7 dB. The suggested antenna gains are 13.4 dBi for C-band, 13.7 dBi for X-band, and 13.4 dBi for Ku-band. Furthermore, the antenna exhibits low cross-polarization and strong isolation, surpassing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25\ dB$</tex>.

articleTitle: Compact Ultra-Wideband Archimedean Spiral Antenna for Electronic Warfare System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized Archimedean spiral antenna is presented having an ultra-wide band (UWB) frequency of operation from 800 MHz to 6 GHz. The spiral antenna is designed taking dual arm Archimedean spiral and the width of the arms has been optimized to get a compact design with a diameter of 130 mm. The proposed antenna shows a larger fractional bandwidth of 152.9 % compared to other spiral antennas in this frequency range. The measured VSWR shows a very good agreement with simulation result. The Archimedean spiral antenna operates from 800 MHz to 6 GHz with a VSWR less than 2:1. The proposed antenna can have wide application such as for global positioning system (GPS), electronic warfare (EW), 5G communication system, weather radar, etc.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Stacked Annular RingAntenna Using Theory of Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)

authors.preferredName: U. V. R. S. S. H. Teja
authors.firstName: U. V. R. S. S. H.

abstract: This paper presents the study of an Annular Microstrip patch antenna using Theory of characteristic modes (TCM). It studies various possibilities of surface current modes propagation on the antenna structure. It further optimizes the port positions for the excitation of the proper modes to achieve the desired radiation pattern. This paper follows a step wise design procedure using TCM as detailed in this paper. The work aims at the design of a wide-band and reconfigurable antennas. The designed antenna operates over 2.4-2.67GHz (260 MHz bandwidth) with a maximum gain of 12dBi. The results are verified with the method of moments (MoM) based commercial solver Altair FEKO.

articleTitle: A Multifunctional FSS with dual band shielding in transmission mode and absorption in reflection mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Here we report a miniaturized frequency selective surface (FSS) which can be used for electromagnetic shielding in the transmission mode in two frequency bands, namely 4.2-5.8 and 8.6-10 GHz. When the same frequency selective surface is placed on a metal backed substrate having the same thickness, it exhibits absorption at 4 and 7 GHz respectively. The multifunctionality in the FSS is brought about without the intervention of active elements which incur high losses. The FSS is designed by the conglomeration of four concentric meandered square loops which resonate at two distinct frequency bands. The transmission and reflection characteristics of the FSS have been analyzed using finite integration technique.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Multidirectional Single Channel Speech Quality Improvement Using Dyadic Discrete Wavelet Transform in Comparison with Discrete Wavelet Transform for Improved Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Innovative dyadic discrete wavelet transform techniques are used to improve multi-directional single-channel speech accuracy. Materials and Methods: The experiment used a Kaggle dataset, which is open-access. The clinic calc tool was used to calculate with a 0.05 alpha, 0.80 G-power, and 0.2 last beta. Group 1 contains Stft and group 2 contains Dwt, each with 376 samples. Thus, 752 samples were used in this experiment. To measure accuracy, 80% of images are trained, 10% tested, and 10% validated, and performance analysis validates SPSS software's better methodology. Results: Dyadic discrete wavelet transform achieved 65% accuracy in speech quality detection and 55% in improvement, with a significance value of 0.001 (P<0.05), resulting in improved sensing performance. Conclusion: Dyadic discrete wavelet transform works better than discrete wavelet transform for speech quality improvement detection.

articleTitle: Analysis of Rotman Lens Geometry for 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
