abstract: Wide area coverage is much demanded in beam-forming applications. Rotman lens is most commonly used for beam-forming among multiple receiver elements. In 5G applications, the conventional lens designs with antenna array does not exhibits good beam coverage due to restricted position of beam and array ports. This research work encompasses the design and analysis of Rotman lens along with microstrip patch antenna array for 5G frequency i.e. 3.45GHz. The simulation of proposed lens structure and microstrip patch antenna array has been done with simulation software CST tool. The proposed Rotman lens design with antenna array offers wide beam coverage area i.e. ±55deg.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Frequency Selective Dual Band Metamaterial Absorber for Mutual Coupling Reduction between MicrostripAntennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-band metamaterial-inspired microwave absorber using a periodic geometry of metal backed frequency selective surface (FSS). The architecture of the FSS unit cell consists of a square ring and a Jerusalem cross, which is printed on a grounded FR-4 substrate. The square unit cell of the FSS has a periodicity of 8.6 mm or 0.072 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> is the wavelength at the lower resonant frequency. The dual-band FSS resonates at 2.5 and 5.17 GHz with absorbtivities of > 96 %. The absorption property of the structure is achieved to be polarization insensitive and high oblique angle stable of > 40°. The 1D array of the absorber unit cells is placed between two microstrip antennas to reduce the surface wave coupling. The absorber-loaded multiple input multiple output (MIMO) array exhibits an isolation improvement of > 20.2 dB and an enhanced return loss bandwidth (BW) of 7.1 % with center at 2.52 GHz.

articleTitle: Wireless Energy Harvesting with Rectenna Technology for Wi-Fi Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a completely novel rectenna design which is capable of collecting RF energy from the popular Wi-Fi band for wireless communications is proposed. A rectenna is a device that can transform RF signals into DC power and is made up of an antenna, a matching circuit, and a rectifier. This rectenna design uses a Schottky diode SMS7630 to complete the rectifier element and lumped components RLC for the antenna portion. To model and improve this design, employ Keysight's Advanced Design Systems (ADS). The Reflection coefficient (S11) and VSWR metrics have been measured, to assess how well this rectenna performs.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Compact and Conformal70 GHz Circular Patch Antenna for V-Band (57-71GHz) 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A single circular antenna resonating at 70 GHz is simulated on a Rogers 5880 substrate with a thickness of 0.252mm. The antenna covers a wide range of frequencies, from 64.00 GHz to 72.00 GHz, with an impedance bandwidth of 6.2 GHz. The electromagnetic energy is radiated by the circular patch, which is connected to a microstrip feedline etched on the top of the dielectric with the full ground on the opposite side. The antenna is ultra-compact, with a small volume of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.5 \times 6\times 0.252\text{mm}^{3}$</tex> on Roger's dielectric material, and has a matching impedance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(49.01-\mathrm{j} 0.23) \Omega$</tex>. The element exhibits a peak gain of 6.08dB at 70.0GHz and a directivity of 5.89dB for the intended frequency band. The compact design, along with a high impedance bandwidth, makes the antenna suitable for high-speed and high-capacity point-to-point and point-to-multipoint wireless links in V-band (57–71GHz) millimeter-wave applications with deployment in 5G infrastructure.

articleTitle: AREA and DELAY Efficient Processing Element Architecture using MBE-WT Adder for CNN Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have become highly accurate and are extensively used for image identification. However, implementing CNNs in hardware creates a substantial challenge due to the proliferation of deep learning applications. Therefore, optimizing hardware design for efficient CNN acceleration is crucial. A vital element of CNN accelerator architecture is the processing element (PE) responsible for carrying out the convolution operation. In this regard, a modified PE design is proposed in this paper aiming to reduce hardware utilization and power consumption. To accomplish this, the paper recommends replacing bulky MAC units and conventional adder trees with a Modified Booth Encoding (MBE) multiplier and WALLACE tree(WT) based adders, respectively. Additionally, the proposed multiplier architecture utilizes XOR MUX full adders instead of conventional full adders. The XOR MUX full adder design requires more logic size than the conventional full adder, but it is more area and power efficient. Verilog HDL was used to implement the suggested design and synthesized on Xilinx Zynq FPGA. The design was compared with conventional approaches in terms of power consumption, area, and delay. The outcome showed that the proposed design outperformed the conventional design, achieving a reduction in area, delay, and power consumption.

articleTitle: Python-Based Graphical User Interface to Extract Electromagnetic Parameters Using NRW Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a python-based (Graphical User Interface (GUI) to extract the permittivity, permeability, impedance and refractive index of a dielectric material from the S-parameters available from the measurements. The Nicolson-Ross-Weir (NRW) algorithm is used to extract the electromagnetic parameters taking into consideration the branching effect. The GUI is user-friendly and users with no background in the electromagnetics can use this extractor. For validating the results CST simulation is performed for homogenous dielectric slabs and inhomogeneous metamaterial. The CST simulated results match with the parameters extracted using the proposed GUI extractor.

articleTitle: A Frequency Domain 8-Bit Chipless RFID tag for IoT and Sensor Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The most anticipated automatic tracking and tagging technology that has emerged in monitoring and locating things in real time over the past decades is Chipless Radio Frequency Identification Technology, whose interrogating signals are electromagnetic. The tag proposed in this paper combines a split ring with hexagonal-shaped resonators. The tag is modeled on FR4 substrate (εr=4.4, tan (j=O.02) having a thickness of 1.6mm which works on frequencies from 1.73GHz to 7.98GHz that helps in IOT and sensor applications. The tag is simulated using CST software and the results are analyzed for the IoT and Sensor applications.

articleTitle: Design of Narrow Edge Liquid Cooled Solid State Pulsed Power Amplifier in X Band With Integrated Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of Narrow edge Liquid cooled Solid State GaN Based Pulsed Power Amplifier with integrated control system. The PA receives the low RF input from exciter unit and provide the sufficient gain in different stages to give the high output RF power over the operational frequency band. It can transfer the heat generated (around 200W) from the GaN devices to the liquid cooled system through thin narrow edge (around 35 mm wide) contact of the Power amplifier. It can work for narrow pulse 100ns to wide pulse 25µs. This module has a FPGA based Monitor & Control card for achieving 100Mbps communication with Radar Controller using LVDS lines. Internal supply to GaN PA devices get cut-off, if the external cover pulse exceeds higher limit of pulse width, thereby preventing the PPA from entering in long pulse width operations & increasing the reliability of the GaN PA devices. The module is designed, fabricated & tested successfully and meets all the required specifications.

articleTitle: A Systematic LHCP Antenna Design Exploration for Smarter IoT Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This manuscript introduces a methodical investigation into the design of left-handed circularly polarized (LHCP) antennas tailored for optimal performance within the framework of Internet of Things (IoT) wireless networks. The envisioned antenna has been crafted using a cost-effective FR-4 substrate with specified dimensions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.603 \lambda\times 0.603\lambda \times 0.0053 \lambda$</tex> (Where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> denotes the free space wavelength at the frequency of 2.59 gigahertz). By the use of circular cross slot parasitic patch mounted on foam spacer over regular truncated antenna, At 2.59 GHz, a heightened gain of 5.27 decibels isotropic (dBi) has been achieved. The proposed antenna can be useful for IoT devices compatible with 5G NR n38 and n41 bands.

articleTitle: A Single/Dual-Polarized $\mathbf{\lambda/4}$ Impedance Transformer Coupled Square Microstrip Patch Antenna for X-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This study introduces compact single-polarized and dual-polarized printed square microstrip patch antennas optimized for SAR applications in the X-band frequency range. The prototypes, named prototype-I and prototype-II, were effectively simulated, fabricated, and measured. Operating at 9.65 GHz with dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{40\mathrm{x}40\mathrm{x}1.587 \ \text{mm}^{3}}$</tex>, they offer impedance bandwidths surpassing 140 MHz (9.56 GHz to 9.7 GHz) with S11 parameters below -10 dB. Prototype-II enhances scattering capability through dual polarization by introducing a horizontal port orthogonal to the vertical port. Measurement results confirm dual polarization achievement at 9.65 GHz, similar to prototype-I. Both prototypes provide low-profile, cost-effective solutions. Prototype-I yields a measured gain of 7.463 dBi with a radiation efficiency of 93%, while Prototype-II achieves gains of 7.345 dBi (vertical port) and 7.302 dBi (horizontal port), with radiation efficiencies estimated at 90.28% and 90.3%, respectively.

articleTitle: A New Defective Ground Structure Inspired High Gain Rectenna System for RF Energy Harvesting in Smart City Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a new rectenna system for RF energy harvesting applications has been proposed. The antenna offers 5.8327 dB of gain. The results obtained demonstrate that the suggested antenna offers a substantial gain of 5.8327 dB and an impedance bandwidth of 1.7183 GHz. The rectifying component incorporates a single series diode (SSD) design, which accurately matches the input impedance by employing L-shaped transmission line matching network. This design choice allows for the efficient utilization of the majority of the received power. The results obtained from the simulation demonstrate that the rectenna achieved a notable conversion efficiency of 68.103% when exposed to a load of 2 kΩ at 3.5 GHz operating frequency and an input power of 5 dBm. The produced output DC voltage is 2.075 V.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Narrowband 28.0GHz n257 and n261 for Short Range Communication with Higher Data Rates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This communication is reported for narrowband MIMO antenna applications at mmWave access applications for n257 and n261. The proposed radiator is evolved and analyzed on RogersRO400340.0GHz dielectric with permittivity=3.55 and thickness of 0.8mm & can be deployed in 5G infrastructure availability. The single-element antenna radiating electromagnetic energy was initiated with radiating patch consisting of a quarter wavelength stub at 28.0GHz connected to a 500 microstrip feed-line and circular-slotted Defected-Ground-Structure (DGS) resulting in a narrowband. This single-element antenna resonated at 28.0GHz with S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>=-45.0dB and offered a corresponding impedance of (50.45-j0.33) Ω with a compact size of 80 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, For achieving higher channel capacity systems, the proposed solo radiator antenna is converted into a 4-port MIMO antenna configuration for radiating electromagnetic waves with a compact volume of 16×20×0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The proposed MIMO antenna can be utilized for mobile networking.

articleTitle: A Novel Broadband 45° Phase Shifter For Space Applications at Ka - Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The paper focuses on design, development and implementation of a 45° phase shifter at Ka-band, 25.5 GHz to 27 GHz, for high data rate transmission for space applications. The phase shifter is designed using both reflection type and load line type topologies. Both the phase shifters are simulated, fabricated and tested. The load line type of phase shifter resulted in better performance compared to the reflection type. Achieved phase shift of 45° and amplitude imbalance of 0.2 dB, low insertion loss of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.5 \text{dB}\pm 0.2\text{dB}$</tex> in the required frequency band.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Non-Woven Polyester Made U Shaped Flexible Patch Antenna for Early Detection of Thyroid Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The U-shaped flexible wearable textile antenna (USWTA) described here serves a critical role in the preliminary diagnosis of cancerous tissues within the thyroid gland. USWTA is crafted from a non-woven polyester as substrate and conducting polyester as a radiating element. USWTA boasts a distinctive design that equips it to discern anomalies within the thyroid gland based on variations in the dielectric properties of the tissues it encounters. When positioned in close proximity to the thyroid gland, the USWTA undergoes notable changes in its operational attributes, encompassing adjustments in parameters such as Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR), Gain, and return loss (S11). These dynamic alterations are meticulously scrutinized to differentiate between cancerous and healthy tissue samples. The selection of a flexible non-woven polyester substrate is a deliberate choice, enabling the antenna to conform to the gland's unique shape while facilitating effective cancer cell detection. Significantly, the antenna exhibits the ability to measure the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) within cancerous cells, a capability that plays a pivotal role in detecting malignancies. USWTA has <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{VSWR \leq 2}$</tex> bandwidth (BW) of 4.5%, 4.66% and 4.7% for on body with cancer, on body without cancer and off-body respectively. USWTA has a peak gain of 9.5 dB at 5.4 GHz with good radiation characteristics. USWTA design is simulated using HFSS software, followed by a validation using a vector network analyzer. Hence the proposed antenna is suitable for wearable and medical device application due to its fast speed.

articleTitle: A Novel Metamaterial Absorber for WiBAN and X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper claims research on a compact ultrathin triple band polarization free metamaterial absorber for microwave frequency applications. Structure resonators make up the preferred absorber unit cell. resonator is imprinted on upper surface of a 0.035 mm thick FR-4 epoxy glass substrate with copper coating on both sides. Under normal incidence, the suggested absorber structure provides three unique Absorption (ABR) peaks. In addition to the foregoing, the suggested absorber structure's Fourfold symmetry makes it polarization independent. In addition, the suggested absorber structure provides more than 90% absorptivity at all angles of frequencies for TE and TM polarization states. The suggested unit cell's ABR process has been explored using E-field distribution, and surface current density (SCD) graphs.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of Metamaterial Absorber using Resistive Loading for X- and Ku-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work proposes a wideband metamaterial-based absorber for X- and Ku-band applications. The designed absorber is a metallic layer loaded with resistors printed on a low-cost FR-4 substrate to obtain the wideband response. The proposed structure has more than 90% absorption over a wide range of frequency bands from 7.68 – 18.82 GHz. This structure is polarization insensitive due to its symmetrical nature and its performance has been analyzed for different incident angles. Angular stability of up to 60-degree angle of incidence has been observed with absorptivity of more than 70% over the entire frequency range.

articleTitle: High Gain AMC- Loaded Millimeter-Wave Antenna for 5G New Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a broadband and high gain antenna, using a novel rectangle truncated corners artificial magnetic conductor. By strategically positioning a rectangle with truncated corners within a larger rectangular ring, the antenna attains notable enhancement in both bandwidth and gain characteristics. The proposed unit cell has zero reflection phase at 47GHz frequency. The AMC configuration has a +90° phase shift at the frequency of 45 GHz and a -90° phase shift at 49 GHz. Hence the bandwidth of the AMC unit cell was 4GHz (f1=45GHz, f2=49GHz). The proposed unit cell with 4x4 AMC array structure integrated with monopole antenna. The antenna produces the -17 dB reflection coefficient and the gain achieved is 7. 15dBi.The antenna is well suited for radio astronomy and the 5G New Radio system.

articleTitle: Design of Wearable Monopole Antenna Sensor for Breast Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper describes the design of a wearable monopole antenna-array sensors for breast tumor detection. The proposed antenna-array comprises four antenna elements and each one is fed individually using micros trip feedline. The antenna is covering the -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 3.2-4.2 GHz with a resonant frequency of 3.7 GHz. To achieve, the conformal property, the proposed antenna-array has been designed on the Rogers RT5880 material of thickness 0.508 mm. The footprint of the proposed array antenna is 0.6λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> × 6.2λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>. This array has been adapted with aim to cover the complete female breast for analysis. The reflection and transmission coefficients studies have been carried out in free space and over breast equivalent phantom. The antenna shows improved intrinsic isolation in presence of tumor. The SAR has been evaluated, and it has been found that input power of 50mW is needed to maintain the SAR-safety guidelines.

articleTitle: Design and Realization of a Compact, Rugged and Highly Efficient Power Supply Module for Large Aperature Antennas in Naval Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Operation of any long range radar involves detection and tracking of targets from a range of thousands of kilometers. It is necessary to use large active aperture array antenna for this purpose with thousands of transmit receive modules which in turn are required to be powered by hundreds of Power Supply Modules (PSMs) in each antenna array. Each such Power Supply Module is required to provide power to optimum number of Transmit Receive Modules (TRMs) co-located within the same Motherboard. Since the mounting, location and the volume available for a PSM within the motherboard is fixed, the PSMs have to be realized within that finite available volume only. At the same time, it has to incorporate an appropriate number of DC-DC converters of requisite output power to provide sufficient power to the TRMs. In this paper, we present the challenges in design and realization of such a compact and rugged PSM which provides input DC power to all its co-located TRMs within the Motherboard and at the same time does not cause any thermal issue owing to its significant heat dissipation. Moreover, the PSM handles multiple types of loads and can command independent switching OFF/ON operation for each load uniquely. The module offers full redundancy in terms of DC-DC converters and ensures high reliability. Besides this, the PSM encompasses a wide variety of protection features. It is qualified as per MIL-STDs and can be seamlessly reused for scaled up applications. The PSM has been realized, qualified, tested and successfully performance evaluated during field trials.

articleTitle: Design of 3.3GHz-3.8GHz 5Watt High Power Amplifier using GaN HEMT Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work presents an approach for the design of high power amplifier based on the load-pull measurement data. The transistor is fabricated using 0.4um GaN on silicon carbide (SiC) process and has a maximum available gain of 21 dB at 3.3 GHz. The power amplifier has been designed by using large-signal equivalent circuit model and load pull measurements. In the power amplifier design, the input and the output impedance matching networks are designed to get the optimum gain and power respectively. The power amplifier biased at drain bias of Ids = 200 mA and Vds = 28 V, gives an output power of 5 Watt with gain of 14dB from 3.3 to 3.8GHz

articleTitle: A Novel Compact Two-Port MIMO Antenna Verified with TCM Analysis for 28/38 GHz 5G mm-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A new miniaturized dual-band multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is designed in this research for usage in 28/38 5G mm-wave wireless communication. The antenna is etched on FR-4 epoxy with size 20.36mm × 8.27mm × 0.4 mm. The proposed antenna is made up of two radiating elements with full ground on the bottom side of the substrate and rectangular slots and stubs on the top side. To enhance isolation, a thin, rectangular stub is positioned in between each MIMO antenna element. The suggested dual-element MIMO antenna functions at a resonance frequency of 28 GHz and 38 GHz, and the isolation between the MIMO components is significantly >33 dB. Peak gains of 4.5 dBi at 28 GHz and 3 dBi at 38 GHz are provided by the antenna, together with radiation efficiencies of >80% at operational bands. Envelope Correlation Coefficient and Diversity Gain are two key MIMO metrics that are studied in order to characterize the performance of the suggested MIMO antenna. The consistent patterns on the E and H planes of the developed antenna make it suitable for 5G applications in the mmwave band.

articleTitle: SOP Minimization in Cooperative Relay-Based NOMA Network with Control Jammer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a new control-jammer (CJ) strategy for improving the secrecy outage probability (SOP) in a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) network with a decode-and-forward (DF) relay. The network configuration involves a source transmitting a composite signal to NOMA users with the assistance of a DF relay. In order to safeguard the users' confidential data from an eavesdropper (Eve), a jammer is deployed. The primary objective of the optimization problem is to minimize the SOP for the NOMA users in the presence of Eve. Under the CJ condition, this paper evaluates the network's physical layer security. Extensive analysis is conducted to compare the performance gap between CJ and other jamming conditions. Through comprehensive simulation results, this study showcases a substantial enhancement in secrecy performance achieved by the proposed CJ scheme at both users, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving the security of the DF relay aided NOMA network.

articleTitle: Simple, Economical & Innovative Solution for Obsolescence Management of Active x3 MIC Based RF Freq Multiplier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper details about practical application of obsolescence management. In this paper MIC based application of RF Built-In Test Equipment (BITE) is discussed where a RF signal from C band is converted to X band signal using an active x3 RF multiplier. The obsolescence of the MMIC based x3 multiplier IC had halted the production of the said BITE module used in EW applications. An alternate economical solution in same real estate and same operative conditions was the need of the hour. The transmitted harmonic power in X band, supply & current consumption, suppression of fundamental frequency in C band, and phase noise aspect are some of the key aspects that was needed for meeting system specification. Thus, an alternative approach which is simple, economical and meeting system specification accommodated in same real estate has been designed and discussed in this paper

articleTitle: Design of Frequency Reconfigurable Dual-Band Rectangular Ring-Shaped Antenna with High Isolation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The proposed MIMO antenna can electronically switch between two frequency ranges. Specifically, it can operate in the (2.14–2.98) GHz range, which is commonly used for Wi–Fi, and the (6.66–7.16) GHz range, which may be used for fixed satellite applications. Two PIN diodes are used in the antenna design to enable the electronic switching between the two frequency ranges. The antenna design incorporates a new inverted F-shaped defective ground arrangement to enhance isolation between the antenna elements. The proposed antenna is simulated using EM solver and obtained a peak realized gains at 2.45 GHz and 6.91 GHz are 4.68 dBi and 4.27 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Triple-Band Efficient Rectifier Circuit for Harvesting Ambient RF-Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The work presents the novel efficient rectifier circuit for harvesting RF energy over 3.34GHz, 4.31GHz, and 5.34GHz resonating frequencies. The projected rectifier consists of 2-stage Dickson charge pump rectifier network with a new model matching unit. The optimized microstrip taper line with open stub and microstrip line combines to form the triple-band matching circuit. ADS tool is used to simulate the rectifier and the results depict the maximum transformation efficiency of 66.17% when all the resonating frequencies are provided at 5dBm input power for an optimum load resistance of 3.5KΩ. The transformation efficiency of the rectifier is above 40% over -5dBm to 12dBm input power range.

articleTitle: Open Ended Slot-Loaded Dual-band Monopole Antenna for WiMAX/ISM-Band/WLAN/sub-6 GHz Applications.
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The paper presents a planar monopole antenna design to achieve dual-band functionality for the application of wireless communication. The design is done using a cost-effective lossy FR4 substrate with dielectric constant 4.4 which is suitable for mass production and implementation. The proposed design is carried out using HFSS (High-Frequency Structure Simulator) software and involves the optimization of important parameters like patch shape, inverted L-shaped slot, partial ground plane and microstrip feed line to achieve dual-band response. The simulated result shows dual-band characteristics response at 3.29 GHz and 5.95 GHz with bandwidths of 3 - 3.6 GHz and 5.2 –7 GHz respectively, making it suitable for the sub-6 GHz 5G (Fifth-Generation) application.

articleTitle: Compact Diplexer Using Electromagnetic Bandgap Resonators for C and X Band Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: For wireless communication, it becomes necessary to employ frequency multiplexing to enable two devices to share a common channel. Diplexers are an example of such microwave devices that facilitate frequency multiplexing. This paper presents an electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure-based new diplexer with two closely located passband resonances at 6.9 and 9.1 GHz. The proposed diplexer displays insertion losses of < 1 dB and 2 dB, whereas the return losses of > 28 dB and 30 dB at the lower and higher frequencies in port-2 and port-3, respectively. Isolation at the output channels is improved by incorporating EBG as coupled resonators to create transmission notches at the two passband frequencies. The total size of the designed diplexer is 35 × 45 × 1.02 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> or 0.8 × 1.03 × 0.02 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> is the free-space wavelength at the lowest resonance. The diplexer will have the potential application to operate at up-link and down-link frequencies of satellite communication, full-duplex, and a radar system in the C and X bands.

articleTitle: Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna-based Feed Cluster with Interlaced Feed Apertures for Satellite Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper introduces a design of a Fabry-Perot Cavity (FPC) based Multi Beam Antenna (MBA) Cluster with enhanced Edge Taper for our specific reflector in S-band. The antenna uses five feeds in conjunction with a high-Q FPC to generate large, interlaced apertures for enhancing on-axis directivities and in turn, Edge Taper of individual feed elements at the required reflector Half Subtended Angles. FPC feeds in a cluster configuration suffer from high Mutual Coupling, and on-axis directivity levels are degraded considerably. That coupling was propitiated in our favour by utilizing matched channel filters, and the on-axis directivity levels were thus re-instituted to single-feed FPCA levels. Thanks to a requirement of all identically polarized feeds, three-channel filters as per channelization requirements were used, but only after the resultant highly dissimilar phase of Mutual Coupling for all feeds was compensated. Only then, the FPC Antenna feeds were matched with the phase of those channel filters, which themselves had a high variation in phase responses (by up to 50°) throughout their adjacent channels. For feeds spaced apart as close as 1λ, on-axis directivity levels better than 15.44 dBi and Edge Taper better than -12.11 dB (greater than -11 dB minima) were achieved.

articleTitle: Design of a Hybrid Frequency and Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna for 5G Sub-6 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A low profile hybrid reconfigurable antenna for sub-6 GHz applications has been reported in this paper. A hybrid, frequency-and pattern-reconfigurable antenna with a semi-elliptical patch make up the design. An inverted L-shaped structure and a defective ground structure (DGS) are put onto the antenna's ground plane. Two PIN diodes are employed in the upper layer to reconfigure frequency, and two diodes are used in the lower layer (ground plane) to achieve pattern reconfigurability. Moreover, the suggested design has a -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 260 MHz for 3.4 GHz-3.6 GHz when the top layer diodes are on and 270 MHz for 3.6 GHz-3.8 GHz when they are off.

articleTitle: A Thin Quad Band FSS Based on Enclosed Cross Slots to Foster Gain in Multiband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The reported work provides a thin-profile quad-band FSS which is designed as a sub-reflector to foster gain in satellite systems, detection systems for sensing traffic light and motion, short-range applications, broadcasting satellite, and direct broadcast satellite. The unit cell spans 0.08λO × 0.08AO × 0.012λo, where, λO is the wavelength corresponding to the lower cut-off frequency. It consists of four stop bands with resonance notes located at 6.6 and 7.98, 9.93 and 12.6, and 20.68 GHz. The FBW of these bands are respectively 60, 9.7, 11.4, and 28.6 %. In addition, fourfold symmetry of the structure results in an excellent response that is insensitive to polarisation and a steady response in both the TE and TM modes. Full wave simulation is used to analyse the structure, and then the measurement of a fabricated prototype is used to verify the results. Multiband wireless technologies can benefit from the reported quadband FSS layer for enhancing gain.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Ultra-Wideband Bandpass Filter with Controlled Band-Notches for Dynamic Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, the implementation of a novel reconfigurable ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter (BPF) is explored. Four distinct operating states are demonstrated, facilitated by the appropriate switching of PIN diodes. In the first operating state, a wide operating range of 3.05-10.62 GHz is achieved through the utilization of a uniform impedance resonator (UIR) loaded with circular stepped impedance stub, coupled with inter-digital (IDG) coupled lines. The second operating state introduces a notch at 7.01 GHz by equipping one arm of the IDG lines with extended vertical stubs. The integration of a cascaded folded stepped impedance resonator (CFSIR) in the circuit extends the BPF's multifunctional capabilities, allowing tri-band operations with notches at 5.1 GHz and 9.7 GHz when used independently. Finally, by combining the CFSIR with vertical stubs in the fourth operating state, quad-band operation is achieved with three notches at 5.1 GHz, 7.1 GHz, and 9.7 GHz. Throughout all operating states, insertion loss remains consistently around −1.5 dB, while group delay remains nearly uniform at less than 0.2 ns within the entire passband. Extensive parametric and analytical studies validate the design concept of the proposed prototype, making it a versatile tool for dynamic frequency control across various applications.

articleTitle: Hexagonal Patch Antenna with Slots and DGS for S and C Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work, a hexagonal patch antenna incorporated with slots and Defected Ground Structure is demonstrated. The hexagonal patch has a side length of 12 mm and an overall antenna dimension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$35\times 36\times 1.6\ \text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. The proposed antenna is operating over a frequency range of (3.27-5.12 GHz) resulting in a bandwidth of 1850MHz. At 3.55 GHz, the antenna's peak gain is measured to be 2.4 dBi. S and C bands are suitable for using the suggested antenna. HFSS software is used to carry out the simulations.

articleTitle: A Compact Antenna Sensor for Diagnosis of Glucose Concentration in Blood Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A compact antenna sensor is designed and developed for the prediction and detection of glucose levels in the blood samples. A human finger phantom consisting of various layers viz; skin layer, bone, blood and fat is devised using simulation environment. The proposed antenna sensor is shown to give variation in frequencies with a peak shift of 6 MHz for each step of glucose variation. The frequency shifts obtained in the designed experiment mapped to the glucose levels in blood samples. The performance of the sensor is analyzed for different locations of real human finger and the resulting resonant frequencies are measured to verify the sensor's performance in real-time scenario.

articleTitle: Smart Blind Glasses Using OpenCV Python
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: With the continuous evolution of technology, the field of object detection has witnessed significant progress. Early techniques relied on hand-crafted features and less precise algorithms, often requiring additional computer vision methods for support. This reliance, however, resulted in suboptimal performance and slow processing speeds. In response to these challenges, this project introduces an end-to-end solution to object detection utilizing an OpenCV Python-based approach. The innovation extends beyond mere visual recognition by incorporating an ESP32 module to convey the detected objects audibly, addressing the accessibility needs of visually impaired individuals. The proposed framework not only streamlines the object detection process but also extends its functionality to identify specific facial features, such as eyes and nose. By eliminating the dependency on external computer vision methods, the system achieves improved efficiency and accuracy. The integration of audio output through the ESP32 module enhances the project's impact, making the information accessible to users with visual impairments. The implementation demonstrates the potential of combining computer vision with versatile hardware solutions for a more inclusive and efficient object detection system.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Bending on Circularly Polarized Textile Reconfigurable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This investigation delves into the impact of bending on a versatile, frequency-adjustable textile antenna. This antenna achieves four distinct configurations by leveraging two BAR-64-03W pin diodes. In standalone conditions, In C1 mode it resonates at various frequencies of 2.4, 4.29, 5.78, and 9.39; in C2 it function at 5 and 5.9; in C3 it operates at 4.4 and 5.8 in C3; and in C4 it resonates at 3.5, 4.4, 5.3. CP occurs at frequencies of 2.4, 3.5, 5.8, and 5.9 GHz within these specified setups. The structural changes induced by bending disrupt the antenna's functionality, prompting an extensive exploration of its electromagnetic behavior variations. Assessing both vertical and horizontal bending effects across these configurations reveals a maximum frequency deviation of 0.35 GHz. Concurrent shifts in axial ratios are also observed. The analyses highlight the antenna's robust performance under diverse human body curvature scenarios.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation and Data Detection using Coarse Quantization for Multiuser MIMO OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) employs multiple carriers, providing significant spectral efficiency, less distortion resulting from multipath transmission. The incorporation of Multiuser Multiple Input Multiple Output (MU-MIMO) with OFDM enables the construction of an efficient method of communication over frequency selectivity channels. The impact of strong interference in the adjacent band on quantized MIMO systems has not been conducted so far. In this paper, coarse quantization-based Maximum-a-Posteriori (MAP) channel estimation and Minimum-Mean Squared-Error (MMSE) data detection methods, was introduced, and their performance trade-offs were investigated. Our research findings indicate that implementing coarse quantization in a MU-MIMO OFDM does not introduce any additional complexity cost in the baseband processing. Moreover, this approach does not lead to any significant performance degradation when compared to the scenario where infinite precision is assumed.

articleTitle: Design of Amplitude and Phase Controlled Butler Beam Forming Network for X/Ku-band Airborne Synthetic Aperture Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Beamforming network plays an important role in today's communication systems. Butler matrix network is one of the useful networks to feed array antenna and to generate multi-beam forming system. Its complexity increases with the increase in number of input and output ports. This research work presentssimulated results of an unequal amplitude 8X8 Butler matrix network with the Taylor series synthesis technique to generate unequal amplitudes (-9.626dB, -9.125dB, -8.798dB, -8.636dB, -8.636dB, -8.798dB, -9.125dB, -9.626dB). The design is going to realize with butler matrix beam forming network based on two frequency bands (X-band and Ku-band) with centre frequency of 9.3GHz and 13.265GHz respectively. The design mainly involves 12 Hybrid couplers and 8 phase shifters which can generate beam in 8 different directions (-32.4°,-26.5°,-15.5°, -10.3°, 10.3°,15.5°, 26.5°, and 32.4°).This design is based on Taylor series expansion which gives an advantage of side-lobe level reduction of -17dB. All the simulations are done in advanced design system software (ADS) key sight technologies. The simulations results are in line with the theoretical calculations.

articleTitle: RFI Survey in L and S Band for APSERa Cosmology Experiment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: We present the results from an RFI (Radio Frequency Interference) survey conducted in the L-band and S-band, as a precursor to building the radio telescope for the APSERa (Array of Precision Spectrometers for the Epoch of RecombinAtion) cosmology experiment. The Epoch of Recombination (ERA) is a phase in the history of the universe, spanning the redshifts 900 < z < 8000, during which the first hydrogen and helium atoms formed. The photons from the recombination process result in additive distortions to the Cosmic Microwave Background spectrum.Feasibility studies have determined that an octave frequency range in the 2–6 GHz band is best suited for a ground-based detection of these cosmological recombination lines. APSERa seeks to detect the same. To determine the potential sites for APSERa, we have developed and deployed a RFI survey system operating in the 500 MHz - 6.5 GHz band across multiple locations in India. The results from the RFI analysis are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 8-Way RF Feeding Network for C-Band Airborne Synthetic Aperture Radar Applications Using Conventional Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)

authors.preferredName: Murali Sesha Sai Nadha Raiu Chakravaram

abstract: This study proposes the design and analysis of an 8-way power divider for unequal division at 5.3 GHz for C band frequency. Many transmission line pieces make up the current power divider. These Transmission lines were printed on a substrate material (RT/duroid 5880, 1.6 mm thick, permittivity 2.2, and loss tangent 0.0002).The 8-way power divider's unequal amplitudes are constructed using Taylor's 1-parameter method to achieve the side projections levels - 17 dB down as from main beam.The proposed power divider consists of using 2 transmission lines with a 3/4 frequency are connected to branched microstriplines, providing excellent isolation and matching between the power divider's two output ports. This power divider is composed of three stages. A 1:2 power divider is used in the first stage, a 1:4 power divider is used in the second stage, and a 1:8 power divider is used in the third stage. According to the simulation results, 1:2 delivers half of the input power, 1:4 produces one-fourth of the power, and 1:8 delivers one-eighth of the input power.All of these assessments were done with the Advanced Design System (ADS) simulation programme. According to both simulated and measured data, the return loss exceeds −35 dB, and the isolation across the output terminals exceeds −40 dB. The proposed circuit operates effectively at C-band frequencies in terms of return loss and isolation (4GHz and 8GHz).

articleTitle: Wearable Button Shaped Antenna for Wireless Body Area Network Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents design and analysis of a button-shaped patch antenna for four different models. The coaxial feed is used for high impedance matching and bandwidth. The button antenna is designed with FR-4 epoxy substrate material. The Model 1 button antenna resonates at a frequency of 6.27GHz, has a reflection coefficient of 20.19dB, provides a bandwidth of 260MHz (6.1307GHz - 6.3920GHz), and the maximum observed gain is 3.24dBi. The Model 2 button antenna resonates at 6.33GHz with a reflection coefficient of -35dB and provides a bandwidth of 260MHz (6.211 GHz - 6.47GHz) and the maximum observed gain is 3.01dBi. The model 3 button antennas resonates at a frequency of 6.33GHz, has a reflection coefficient of -49dB, and provides a bandwidth of 240MHz (6.21GHz - 6.45GHz) and a maximum observed gain of 5.13dBi. The Model 4 button antenna resonates at 5.8844 GHz frequency respectively with a reflection coefficient of -26.5dB and offers the Bandwidth of 210MHz (5.76GHz - 5.97GHz) and the maximum gain observed as 5.19dBi. The radiation patterns are observed as semi-omni directional. The compact design proves the antenna suitable for wearable WBAN applications.

articleTitle: A Planar ɸ-Shaped Microwave Antenna Sensor for Glucose Concentration Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work presents a non-invasive method for observing the glucose concentration variations by using a proposed planar ϕ-shaped antenna sensor. The proposed microstrip antenna is resonating at a frequency of 4 GHz. The proposed antenna is fabricated on low-cost FR-4 substrate of size 22mm×30mm×1.6mm. At resonating frequency 4 GHz a finger phantom of real human is designed with various layers like skin, fat, blood and bone in electromagnetic simulation tool. At various locations around the proposed antenna the finger phantom is situated and corresponding frequency shifts are noted to evolution of concentration of glucose variations from 0 mg/dL to 1000 mg/dL. The frequency shift of maximum 75 MHz is obtained when the phantom of the finger is placed at the top of the proposed antenna sensor parallel to feed and in the remaining cases the frequency shift is obtained but it is minimum.

articleTitle: A Compact Planar Antenna Operating at Lower and Higher 5G Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a compact planar antenna that can operate at both lower sub 6 GHz bands and as well as at higher 5G bands. The antenna consists of q shape monopole with eight L shaped spokes inside the radiator. The feed line is asymmetrical about the radiator. The ground plane is made defective resembling rectangle shape. The antenna has dimensions of 9.5*15*1.6 mm3. As the antenna is of compact size, it finds applications in 5G devices.

articleTitle: Study on Quantum Radars for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The need for improved and reduced integration time for detection in radars has led researchers to develop quantum radars. Quantum Radars use the concepts of quantum mechanics, like quantum entanglement and quantum illumination to give enhanced results in detection with reduced integration time. Quantum Radars have found applications in various fields like - aerospace, biomedical imaging, and civilian. This paper primarily focuses on the novel design of a quantum antenna that is capable of simulating the phenomena of quantum entanglement. It also gives a concise idea about Quantum radars by providing a comparison to the classical radars and a simple simulation of a quantum antenna that can be used to create the phenomena of quantum entanglement.

articleTitle: A Non-Invasive Glucose Monitoring Using Double S-Shaped Antenna Band Stop Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work propose a double S-shaped antenna band stop filter and it has been chosen a defected ground structure (DGS) as a sensor for prophesy glucose concentration evaluation in human blood. The proposed microstrip antenna has two ports and it resonating frequencies are 3.216 GHz and 5.66 GHz. The proposed antenna filter has a size of 42 mm × 16 mm. The electromagnetic simulation environment is used for designing the real human finger phantom model at two resonating frequencies with different layers like skin, fat, blood and bone. Evaluating the concentration of glucose, it varies from 0 mg/dL to 1000 mg/dL and the corresponding shifts in frequency are identified by situating the finger at center position of the proposed antenna filter. The maximum shift in frequency of 132 MHz is obtained at the phantom is designed at 5.66 GHz and a minimum shift in frequency of 24 MHz is obtained at the phantom designed at 3.216 GHz.

articleTitle: RF Front End Combinational Filter for Airborne V/UHF Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The RF front-end filter within an airborne communication system plays a crucial role in the selection of desired signals, the rejection of interference, and the preservation of signal quality. Front end filter is essential for ensuring effective and reliable communication between aircraft and ground stations, thereby enhancing safety and operational efficiency in aviation. The proposed solution involves a combination of RF front-end filters to separate various interferences, including low-pass, high-pass, and band-stop filters. This comprehensive filter design covers a wide frequency range, spanning from Very High Frequency (VHF) to Ultra-High Frequency (UHF), ranging from 30MHz to 600MHz, and incorporates a band-stop filter between 88MHz and 118MHz. This design is particularly well-suited for Software Defined Radio (SDR) receivers used in airborne applications, supporting aviation, maritime, and military communications. The design is implemented on a Printed Circuit Board (PCB) made of Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), and the test results align closely with the simulation results, offering a promising solution for airborne tactical communication systems.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-Wave Array Antenna for Improvement of Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A key component of contemporary wireless communication systems, millimeter wave (mm Wave) antenna arrays allow for the achievement of high-speed data transfer, low-latency connection, and large device density for the next generation of wireless networks. An overview of mm Wave antenna arrays is provided in this work, with particular attention paid to their design, properties, and uses. The essential ideas of millimeter-wave (mm Wave) communication are covered, together with the special propagation properties and difficulties brought on by higher frequencies. The benefits and drawbacks of various antenna array layouts, including uniform linear arrays (ULA), uniform rectangular arrays (URA), and other sophisticated arrangements, are discussed.

articleTitle: Reflector-based Isolation Technique for mm-Wave MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work is focused on mutual coupling reduction among the antenna ports at mm-wave frequencies, which are frequencies of interest for 5G communication. Initially, the design and simulation of a single-port T-shaped wideband antenna resonating at 26 GHz with a frequency range of 24–28 GHz have been presented for possible Multiple Input and Multiple Output (MIMO) applications. The single-port wideband antenna has been extended to four-ports, and a reflector approach has been utilized to lessen mutual coupling. This isolation strategy reduces the mutual coupling by 5 dB, which is verified through software simulations. The isolation enhancement is also verified using surface current distributions.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Volumetric Antenna using SIW Technology loaded with DGS for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Single band volumetric antenna loaded with Defected Ground Structure (DGS) using Substrate Integrated Waveguid e (SIW) technology is presented. With a dielectric constant of 4.4, the antenna's dimensions are 51.5 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$*40$</tex> mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$*1.6$</tex> mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{L}^{*}\mathrm{W}^{*}\mathrm{h})$</tex> and it is made of FR4 (Flame Retardant) substrate material. By varying the ground plane's lengths (Lg1 and Lg2), the HFSS antenna simulation tool analyses the reported antenna's properties. The simulation result shows gain of 5.89 dB and direction of maximum radiation 4.57 at the radiating frequency of 12.60 GHz. The projected volumetric SIW antenna structure provides a wider bandwidth of 1.75GHz. It is widely used in radio astronomy, defence systems and spacecraft in the Ku band, among other areas.

articleTitle: Generation of High-Gain Steered Beam using Dipole Antenna Loaded on Anomalous Reflector with Near-field Correction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a binary coded anomalous reflector with near-field correction technique is proposed for generation of directive beam from a dipole antenna. The proposed anomalous reflector of dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10\lambda_{0}\times 10\lambda_{0}$</tex> operates at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f=5.9GHz$</tex> and is capable of simultaneously correcting for near-field effects, while characteristically bearing a phase gradient to steer the main beam towards a designed angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$45^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex>. First, the phase gradient for far-field incidence is computed using generalised Snell's law. Next, the phase gradient is modified accordingly to correct the near-field effects due to the radiator placed at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}/4$</tex> above the anomalous reflector. The proposed anomalous reflector is designed on an FR-4 substrate. The primary radiator is a printed dipole with integrated balun matched to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50 \Omega$</tex>. The dipole is designed on RT Duroid substrate of thickness 0.508mm. The placement of dipole with anomalous reflector along two orientations is studied for Gain and HPBW, and is compared to a dipole with PEC bearing the same dimensions. The dipole is individually optimised with both the PEC and the anomalous reflector to achieve optimum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> and impedance matching. For the anomalous reflector with dipole, a peak gain of 14.8 dBi is observed while consequently steering the beam at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$45^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex>. The proposed dipole backed with near-field corrected anomalous reflector can be employed in applications like Vehicle to Vehicle (V2V) or Vehicle to Everything (V2X) networks.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Compact Microstrip Patch Antenna with DGS for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The Research paper aimed to explore the potential of Defective Ground Structures (DGS) in enhancing the capabilities of a microstrip patch antenna with a rectangular patch having an insert feed that resonates at 4.5 GHz. The results were impressive. The return loss was significantly decreased by −33 dB, and the bandwidth was increased from 700 MHz to 1.3 GHz. Furthermore, by incorporating DGS, the antenna gained an extra of 0.5dB, particularly at the 4.5 GHz frequency. The reduction in reflected power (to −33 dB) is crucial for efficient signal transmission, which is fundamental to wireless communication. The amplified gain of the antenna demonstrates its ability to strengthen signal strength, making it an ideal choice for applications that require top-notch performance in 4.5 GHz frequency wireless communication systems. Our research measures the effectiveness of using Defective Ground Structures in enhancing the performance of microstrip patch antennas, especially in the 4.5 GHz range.

articleTitle: Compact Rotman Lens on Water Based Substrate for Low-Frequency Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The Rotman lens is an inexpensive, less complex, compact, wideband and easy to fabricate analog beam former used extensively for producing multiple beams in the sky for simultaneous observation over a wide field of view. It is expected to play a major role in low frequency applications where physical dimensions are not easily manageable because of large wavelength involved. We have developed a new methodology of making the Rotman lens compact by a factor of a little over 8 when compared to vacuum by designing it on an in-house developed water based composite dielectric medium which has an effective dielectric constant of about 26.8. A Rotman lens has been designed and developed on this dielectric medium to produce two beams at ~ ±30 deg. around zenith along with a beam at the centre in the frequency range of 100–200 MHz. A prototype has been constructed to demonstrate the concept with the help of a three element antenna array.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Planar 3 × 3 Nolen Matrix for Beamforming Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The design and analysis of a 3 × 3 Nolen matrix centered at 2 GHz is presented in this paper and measured results are compared with simulation data. The designed 3 × 3 Nolen matrix consists of hybrid couplers and phase shifters arranged in a triangular lattice, when exciting any one of the input ports from the three input ports it produces the unique phase difference of -90°, 150° and 30°. It is modeled and, simulated using Ansys HFSS and the MATLAB RFPCB Toolbox ™, and fabricated by using the dielectric FR4 epoxy. The simulated reflection parameter at each port is better than 10 dB at a desired frequency compatible with the measured results. With good progressive phase shift capability, the presented Nolen matrix can be suitable feed network for beamforming antenna applications.

articleTitle: Wrist Band Antenna for Wireless Body Area Network Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work a miniaturized CPW-fed wearable and flexible antenna is designed and analyzed in free space, cylindrical bend and simulated human hand models. Kapton Polyimide is used as a substrate material. The dielectric constant (Cr) is equal to 3.4 and height (h) is equal to 0.1 mm is considered. The miniaturized CPW-fed antenna resonates at 1.9 GHz and 4.4 GHz frequencies when placed in free space, 1.88GHz and 4.3 GHz frequency with cylindrical bend and 4.7 GHz frequency when placed on hand. The reflection coefficients (S11) are observed as -22.278 dB, -27.92 dB for free space, -27.94 dB and -15.9 dB, for cylindrical bend, and -18 dB for on hand models. The bandwidths observed as 0.84GHz (1.49 to 2.33 GHz),1.21GHz (3.79 to 5.0 GHz) for free space with a gains of 2.32 dBi, 2.97 dBi respectively. For cylindrical bend the bandwidth observed as 0.79GHz (1.43 to 2.22 GHZ), 1.06GHz (3.78 to 4.84GHz) with a gain of 2.23dBi, 2.65dBi and for on hand condition 0.92GHz (4.2 to 5.12GHz) bandwidth is observed with a gain of -16.3 dBi. The radiation patterns observed as directional and semi-directional and bi-directional. CST v 2019 software is used for designing and simulation of proposed antenna. According to design analysis the proposed antenna is good for WBAN applications.

articleTitle: EM Design of Beam Steering Antenna using Active Frequency Selective Surfaces at 24 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A beam steering antenna using active frequency selective surfaces (AFSS) has been proposed in this paper. The antenna is designed to operate in the K-band. A U-shaped microstrip patch antenna has been placed below an AFSS layer. The beam is being steered by ON and OFF state of the PIN diodes that are embedded onto the unit cells of frequency selective surface structure that is used as superstrate of antenna. The proposed antenna can achieve a maximum beam tilt of 32º and a maximum gain of 7.28 dB by changing the state of the PIN diodes. The proposed design can find its application in radar altimeter employed for space applications due to its light weight.

articleTitle: Systematic Analysis of a RF-Choke Enabled 2-Bit Reconfigurable Digitally Coded Metasurface for 5G Beam Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A RF-choke enabled 2-bit reflect metasurface unit cell has been proposed with a highly improved reflection efficiency for all 4 possible diode states (‘00’, ‘01’, ‘10’, and ‘11’) with almost equi-spaced reflection phase responses (‘121°’, ‘42°’, ‘−47°’, and ‘−125°’). Different reflection phase responses can be achieved from the same unit-cell using the switching mechanism of ON-OFF states of the two SMP1340_079 pin-diodes. RF-Choke circuit is added as part of the biasing network of the meta-atom to achieve the high reflection efficiency up to 92%. Then, the reconfigurable metasurface is implemented with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$12\times 12$</tex> arrangement of the proposed unit cell and illuminated with a horn keeping the f/d ratio of 0.8. The scattered field by the metasurface with changing phase gradients using various coding patterns, is predicted by a semi analytical method for different target angles (−60°, −30°, 0°, +30°, +60°) for 5G beam steering application.

articleTitle: A Wearable Textile Antenna for Health Care Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper explores the utilization of diverse materials, including denim, cotton, jeans, leather, and silk, as substrates in antenna design. Specifically tailored for biomedical and healthcare applications, a novel textile antenna employing a denim substrate operates within the 2.4363GHz-2.5236GHz frequency band, centered at 2.47GHz. The antenna demonstrates a commendable gain of 6dB and an efficiency reaching approximately 65%, rendering it highly suitable for healthcare-related implementations. Utilizing the CST Tool, rigorous simulations and subsequent fabrication of the suggested antenna were conducted. The simulated reflection coefficient stands at −28dB, surpassing the benchmark of −10dB, indicative of strong performance and a robust impedance matching characteristic. Comparative analysis across the five substrates further delineates the strengths of the proposed denim-based antenna. This research lays a solid foundation for the advancement of textile-based antennas in healthcare applications, showcasing the viability and efficacy of such designs while providing valuable insights into material suitability for future innovations in this domain.

articleTitle: Tumor Identification and Classification of MRI Brain Images Using Deep Learning Optimizers (Adam vs Sgdm)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Diagnosing brain tumors presents a complex and challenging task for medical professionals. It requires accurate detection and classification of tumor volume, which is essential for determining the appropriate treatment. In recent times, deep learning algorithms, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have shown the best results in medical image analysis. For our study, we utilized a CNN-based method to detect brain tumors by analyzing MRI scans. The use of Deep Learning for segmenting and classifying tumors presents an excellent improvement nowadays both in identification and classification. In this project, we studied the application of two popular deep learning optimizers namely Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation) and SGD with Momentum (Sgdm), to improve the accuracy and efficiency of tumor identification and classification from MRI brain images By comparing the performance of these optimizers, we aim to elucidate their effectiveness in the context of medical image analysis. Here the classification of BTs into 4 classes (Normal, Pituitary Tumor, Meningioma Tumor, Glioma Tumor). For training purposes, T1-weighted images are used. The testing accuracies for both Deep Learning optimizers achieve 98-99 % with variation in time and learning parameters. The proposed algorithm signifies the classification outcomes of many state-of-art-methods.

articleTitle: Sustainable Design and Analysis of a Quasi Snowflake Fractal Antenna for Multiband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a sustainable quasi hybrid snow flake fractal antenna at 2.4 GHz is designed and modified to acts as a multiband antenna is presented. The antenna consists of a radiating patch in the shape Quasi Koch Snowflake Sierpinski Gasket structure with slots inside. The antenna geometry shape is based on third iteration of Koch Snow Flake with The antenna is fed with a 50 ohms coaxial feed at the appropriate position for proper impedance matching. The proposed antenna is designed on FR4 substrate having dielectric constant 4.4 and thickness 1.6 mm and area of 60mm X 60 mm. The proposed antenna is analysed using Ansys/HFSS software. The presence of slots in the third iteration of proposed antenna is responsible for the multiband operation in addition to the Koch Snow Flake structure. The proposed antenna is fabricated and tested. The proposed antenna attained maximum bandwidth of 0.6GHz, and peak gain 6.75 dBi. This antenna is suitable for multiband applications for present wireless communications and the structure can be integrated with other circuit components as the antenna is planar. The simulated and measured results are in consistent with the theory.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis Assisted Power Handling Capability Enhancement in Probe-Fed Microstrip Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: An investigation into enhancing the power handling capability (PHC) of probe-fed microstrip patch antennas, for high-power applications, in the UHF range, is presented. The method involves substituting conventional SMA connectors, commonly used as microstrip antenna feeds, with tapered coaxial connectors featuring constant longitudinal impedance. The maximum PHC(s) of the antennas, with the tapered connector feeds, are identified by integrating full-wave simulations with thermal analysis of the models, through Altair HyperStudy. Microstrip patch antennas designed on RT-duroid <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{r}=2.2,\ \tan\delta=0.0009)$</tex> and TMM-10i <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\epsilon_{r}=9.8,\ \tan\delta=0.002)$</tex> substrates, utilizing the tapered connector feeds, exhibited PHC <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\approx 4\ \mathbf{kW}$</tex> and 6 kW, respectively, marking a significant improvement compared to SMA connectors, which typically handle only a few <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100\mathrm{s}$</tex> of watts of input peak power.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Cost Compact FR-4 Microstrip Patch Antenna for 5G, ISM, and X-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This study focuses on advancing low-cost patch antenna technology, specifically exploring a rigid model fine-tuned for 5G and Satellite Communication Applications through the utilization of FR-4 as the substrate. Emphasizing compactness, the engineered antenna boasts dimensions of 25mm × 25mm × 1.5mm for the rigid variant, demonstrating meticulous design with circular structures forming both patch and ground elements. Noteworthy is the deliberate optimization for concentric shapes within the radiating structures. The FR-4 antenna proves its versatility by operating across multiple frequencies—spanning 2.1GHz, 3.8GHz, 5.8GHz, and 8.4GHz—paving the way for diverse applications encompassing n1 5G, LTE 5G, ISM, and X-band functionalities.

articleTitle: Compact Flexible Textile Antenna for Microwave Imaging of the Human Head
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The present study involves the construction of a compact, flexible textile antenna made on cotton substrate for Microwave Brain Imaging (MBI). The structure that is constructed exhibits an operational frequency range spanning from 1.7 to 7 GHz, with a matching performance that exceeds 10 dB. The antenna achieves a peak gain of 3.98 dBi while operating at a frequency of 6.7 GHz. The evaluation of the impact of the antenna on the human head involves the examination of the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) of the planned antenna. The process involves the creastion of a head model consisting of seven distinct layers. The assessment of Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) is conducted by activating various antennas in a multistatic configuration. All the performance characteristics of the proposed structure were carefully examined from the simulator.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Fed Dielectric Rod Filtenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a dielectric rod fitenna is proposed in x-band. To get the filtering characteristics, a Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) based band pass filter is used to feed the dielectric rod through a slot. The proposed structure is exhibiting a band width of 4% at 10 GHz. The peak gain is 9 dBi in the operating band for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\lambda 0$</tex> long dielectric rod radiator. The gain of the proposed antenna can be increased using longer length of radiator.

articleTitle: Rectangle Patch Antenna with Slots and Defective Ground Structure for C-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a rectangle patch antenna with slots and defective ground structure. The proposed antenna has overall dimensions of 36×39×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The rectangle patch antenna with pentagonal and hexagonal slots was designed. Further to improve the bandwidth and gain defective ground structure is incorporated. The operating frequency range from 5.47-6.11GHz with a bandwidth of 640MHz. Applications in the C-band are appropriate for the antenna. Ansys HFSS was used to conduct the simulations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Slot and Via Position Effects on Bandgap Characteristics in Mushroom Electromagnetic Bandgap Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Electromagnetic bandgap structures (EBG) are artificial periodic elements designed to prevent electromagnetic (EM) waves from propagating within certain frequency ranges. The combination of EBG structures with antennas improves overall performance by effectively reducing surface waves generated by the antennas within a specified frequency band. The standard Mushroom EBG unit cell was studied using HFSS software at a resonance frequency of 5.2 GHz. MEBG consist of via at center which connects the metallic patch and substrate. This paper investigates the influence of introducing slots and adjusting the positioning of the via on the bandgap characteristics and resonant frequency within the EBG structure.

articleTitle: A 2-bit Polarization-Insensitive Unit Cell for Triple Band Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a unit cell of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) that is polarization-insensitive, tunable, and stable even for oblique incident signals in multi-frequency bands with very low absorption. A low loss substrate has been utilized to design the unit cell. The unit cell consists of a plus-shaped patch inside a square-shaped metal loop connected by four symmetrically arranged varactor diodes on the top surface and the bottom surface is covered with a metal sheet. A via is placed in the center of the unit cell connecting the top and bottom surface through the substrate. By changing the capacitance of the diodes various phase shifts in S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> has been obtained. The proposed design is simulated for the center frequencies of each frequency band (3 GHz, 5.2 GHz, and 6.2 GHz), and the results show that the design is insensitive to polarization and can cover 360° phase in 90° intervals. Phase variation remains constant up to 70° for TE and 20° for TM polarized incident signals.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of 3GPP-Standard Driven Polar Coded Modulation for 5G
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work provides a comparative study of the 5G new radio (NR) polar coding with different symbol modulation techniques and different delay profiles of NLOS channel. It has been observed that for the same remaining configurations, the block error rate and the block length error rate performances require higher amount of bit to noise ratio in 16-QAM modulation compared to the BPSK and QPSK modulation in both uplink and downlink transmission scenarios. In the next section, the impact of modulation on the signal received in a physical downlink control channel have been studied for different tapped delay profiles. The reported analyses carried out using the 3GPP guideline based 5G new radio model blocks of MATLAB 5G Toolbox can be further utilized for designing standard based 5G waveforms in different practical scenarios.

articleTitle: Design of Integrated Hexagonal Microstrip Patch Antenna with DGS for Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: IoT (Internet of Things), 5G systems are being developed and advancement in aerial radiating in high frequency spectrum bands in GHz. This paper concentrating on Parametric analysis of multi number of hexagonal micro strip patches are integrated and applied Defective Ground Structure (DGS) method. The proposed antenna dimensions are 28mm width and 32mm length with FR4 substrate used as a dielectric material with height of 1.6mm. Explore various design iterations, notified that the best results are harvested using multi hexagonal shaped patches and DGS technique for this suggested design structure. Return loss (S11) parameter value is analysed. The antenna resonates at 16.45GHz with return loss of -23.13dB.Peak gain is observed 7.28dB at 16.45GHz, Voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) 1.14 and at 16.45GHz. Input impedance at 50Ω, current and electric field distributions are noticed. The projected antenna is significantly suitable for wideband applications.

articleTitle: CX Band Semi Disk-Ring Dual Band Shared Aperture Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: An efficient simple design of a dual band low isolation shared aperture antenna is presented in this communication. The design consists of a semi disk placed in between a circular ring with a two port network. The S-parameters have shown good response of -40 dB in the band with a directivity/gain of about 7.8 dBi. The side lobe levels have been reduced to an ultralow level of -29.1 dB. The designed antenna resonates in C and X frequency bands and the isolation is as low as -35 dB and -45 dB respectively at the two resonating frequencies.

articleTitle: Aperture Coupled High Gain Metasurface Based Antenna for CP Radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A two-layered, low-profile aperture coupled high-gain meta-surface (MS) based antenna with circularly polarized (CP) radiation is investigated in this paper. The planar MS consists of uniform metallic patch cells fed by an aperture of a circular-shaped slot joined with two side arm slots and a plus-shaped micro-strip line at the bottom of the substrate. Meanwhile, the MS is elaborately designed to provide higher gains for different values of the external patch cells. The MS also works as a highly efficient radiator, by enhancing impedance bandwidth, gain and also providing CP radiation.
