The operating bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 1.5 GHz (4.83 GHz-6.33 GHz), and the axial ratio bandwidth is 1.05 GHz (5.1 GHz-6.15 GHz) centered at 5.5 GHz frequency, which is suitable for WLAN applications. The simulations show that a high gain of 8.36dBic is obtained at 5.5 GHz frequency.

articleTitle: Multiuser Precoded OFDM System over Nonlinear Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The presence of a nonlinear power amplifier (NPA) in an orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system can introduce distortion and spectral regrowth, leading to the degradation of the system's signal quality and an increase in interference. In this paper, we investigate the impact of NPA in multi-user multiple-input multiple-output OFDM (MU-MIMO-OFDM) systems operating over finite impulse response (FIR) and infinite impulse response (IIR) fading channels. MU-MIMO-OFDM systems are sought after for their high data rates and spectral efficiency. However, in the downlink MU-MIMO-OFDM system, performance degradation occurs when nonlinear conditions manifest in the transmitter's NPA, especially with an increasing number of users. This degradation is reflected in the bit error rate (BER) performance. To mitigate this issue, we explore the application of multiuser precoding in the MU-MIMO-OFDM system to reduce interference in signal detection. We analyze BER performance while considering various system parameters, including the number of users, transmitting and receiving antennas, and NPA parameters. Our findings reveal that NPA, especially when combined with IIR, significantly degrades system performance and saturates the BER in high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regions.

articleTitle: Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna Array for 5G mmWave Applications at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper antipodal Vivaldi antenna (AVA) array is proposed for fifth generation mmWave applications. The proposed AVA array consists of 1×4 antenna elements and with dimensions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$55.3\times 26.6\times 0.79\text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. The antenna is designed using Rogers RT/duroid 5880 material having dielectric constant 2.2 and this material have low dielectric losses and is suitable for high frequencies. Triangular corrugations, rhombus parasitic patches and SIW (substrate integrated waveguide) are used in antenna design for improvement of gain, bandwidth, and low radiation losses. The proposed antenna is operating from 25.78 GHz–30.74 GHz frequency range and antenna is resonating at 28.56 GHz. Gain is varies from 9.45 to 14.88 dBi in specified frequency band. The proposed antenna is designed using ansys HFSS tool.

articleTitle: Detection of Brain Stroke by using the Novel Adaboost Classifier Algorithm Classifier Algorithm Compared with Multi-layer Perceptron
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Compare Novel Adaboost Classifier Algorithm and MultiLayer Perceptron to improve accuracy. Materials and Methods: Research groups include Novel Adaboost Classifier Algorithm and MultiLayer Perceptron. The 64.4 MB dataset includes 30 healthy and 30 damaged brain images. Kaggle provided CT images for brain stroke detection. Identifying the training dataset requires 500 records-80% for training and 20% for testing. A unique Adaboost method and a multilayer perceptron approach were compared using 10 sets to improve research accuracy. Ten times per iteration, twenty sets were compared. The G power test with α=0.05 and β=0.2 yields approximately 80%. A novel Adaboost classifier algorithm (88.84%) beats MultiLayer Perceptron (83.40%). The independent sample test value is significant at 0.01 (p<0.05). Study: Novel Adaboost Classifier beats Multi-Layer Perceptron. Two accurate brain stroke categorization algorithms were found. A dataset verifies results. Different datasets may affect it.

articleTitle: Dual Band Symmetrical Semi Cylindrical DRA with Patch Antenna for C and X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper two element symmetrical semi cylindrical DRA are placed on the top of the patches with symmetrical in shape of semi-circle patch elements. This antenna is operating in Multiple frequencies with good impedance matching. The DRA antenna is operating at 6.3GHz, 6.9GHz, 8.1GHz and 9.2GHz with S-Parameters -19.61dB, -2253dB, -19.71dB and -19.91dB. The band width at two bands are 1.08GHz and 1.8GHz in X-Band applications.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Small Reflector Antenna Design for Satellite Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Small steerable reflector antennas are of prime importance on scientific satellites to transmit the experimental data towards the ground station. However, achieving higher efficiency and having minimum dynamic envelop during the rotation is a challenging task. In this paper, design of a reflector with diameter 28λ at X-band in Axially Displaced Ellipsoid (ADE) geometry is illustrated. It is experimentally demonstrated that the antenna can provide an aperture efficiency of more than 70% which is significant especially considering the small diameter of the reflector. This efficiency has been achieved by proper choice of design parameters and material used. Thermo-plastic based struts are used to support sub-reflector from the feed.

articleTitle: A Four-Port Super-Wideband Monopole Antenna Including Multi-Band Wireless Applications for On-Body Applications with SAR Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This communication reports the analysis of single, and four-port MIMO antenna with super-wideband characteristics. Including bandwidths of 8.32GHz-71.89GHz & 7.84GHz-73.292GHz respectively. The proposed antenna is designed on very thin RF-substrate and its four-port MIMO antenna design occupies space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$24\times 24 \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. The impedance-bandwidth includes multiple narrow-bands such as X-Band, Ku-Band, K-Band, Ka-Band, Q-Band, U-Band and V-Band. The annular-ring forms the radiating patch printed on top-surface and defected-ground (DGS) on opposite surface. The proposed work is also subjected to SAR analysis for On-Body applications.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Quantification of the Gain Budget for INCUS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: INCUS (INvestigation of Convective UpdraftS) is an Earth Science project approved by NASA in 2022. The goal of the mission is to study in detail how water vapor and droplets move inside tropical storms and thunderstorms and understand their effects on weather and climate models. To carry out this study, the mission will use three almost identical SmallSats, each one equipped with a Ka-band radar heritage of Raincube. The deployable mesh reflector antenna is a new 1.6m design provided by Tendeg. The bus for each of the three observatories is provided by Blue Canyon Technology (BCT), while Colorado State University leads the science team of the project. This paper presents the general architecture of the three observatories with particular emphasis on the radar antenna subsystem design. In particular, a statistical analysis to evaluate the impact of fabrication tolerances of the deployable mesh reflector surface and their effect on the antenna gain will be presented.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Bandpass Filter using Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative dual-band bandpass filter (BPF) design utilizing two Asymmetrical Ushaped multimode resonators. This filter is assembled by combining a U-Shaped Asymmetrical Resonator (USAR) and a pair of coupled transmission lines. The two USARs define the first and the second passbands. This arrangement provides exceptional design flexibility, effectively providing various design specifications. Our dual-band BPF has been meticulously designed and thoroughly simulated. The simulation results reveal that the two passbands are centered at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.40\text{GHz}$</tex> and 5.0 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GHz}$</tex>, each with fractional bandwidths of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.75{\mathrm{\% }}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9.4{\mathrm{\% }}$</tex>, respectively. These resonating bands have promising potential for modern wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Slotted Microstrip Patch Antenna for Wide-Band Applications with Controlled Resonance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This research paper presents a comprehensive study of the design, simulation, and analysis of a slotted microstrip patch antenna intended for wide-band applications. The design achieved a wide band from 10.5GHz to 14GHz. Primarily the antenna is designed for 7.5GHz where the antenna shows 600 MHz bandwidth. The antenna shows excellent return loss of -22.5dB at 7.5GHz and wideband too. The proposed slotted microstrip patch antenna emerges as a promising candidate for wide-band applications, demonstrating controlled resonance within the designated frequency band while supporting diverse communication needs. The radiation patterns of the antenna show uniform radiation in both the upper and lower hemispheres. The antenna shows a gain of 4.7dBi and the antenna is used for various medical applications.

articleTitle: A Compact and Wide Band Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A compact and geometrically simple millimeter wave antenna is proposed and discussed in this work. The suggested design contains an inverted L-shaped stub and a circular ring-shaped stub. The antenna is fed at the left corner of the substrate material Rogers 6002. The purpose of the stubs is to increase the antenna's bandwidth and return loss. Furthermore, the antenna operates at the resonance frequency of 28 GHz and provides wideband with a high gain up to 10 dBi. Additionally, antenna results are compared to recent research works. Based on the comparison and outcomes, the presented antenna is an excellent choice for future compact devices operating in the millimeter wave spectrum.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Improvement of Bowtie Antenna Using Annular Ring for Vehicle-to-Vehicle Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In the present work, a novel bowtie antenna with radiation pattern improvement using annular ring is presented for vehicle-to-vehicle communication. The proposed leaf-shaped bowtie antenna resonates in the frequency band 2.4 to 6.8 GHz with good reflection characteristics meeting Wi-Fi, WLAN and V2X bands. The important characteristic of V2X communication is to have omnidirectional radiation pattern on azimuthal plane. The design of the proposed antenna is improved by adding annular ring to get the desired omnidirectional radiation pattern. The developed antenna meets the IEEE 802.11p standards and can be easily integrated into vehicles.

articleTitle: Design and Comparative Study on Planar ELC Resonators for ϵr Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This article presents design of three types of Electric LC resonators based on primitive shapes. The rectangular, circular and hexagonal shaped structures are considered for design and analysis. The footprint of each resonator is 40 × 40 × 1.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> which is designed on FR-4 substrate with relative permittivity of 4.4 and loss tangent of 0.02. The resonator characteristics are obtained through EM simulations performed in Ansys Electromagnetics (AEDT –HFSS) and presented in terms of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>, and phase response. Further, a dielectric superstrate is placed on the top of the resonator and the variation of resonant frequency characteristics were noted with different ϵ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> variations.

articleTitle: Performance of Multiple Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces in RF and FSO Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Relay assisted wireless communication systems has been considered as a key technique to extend the network coverage and enhance QoS. To study the significance of relays in the Free Space Optics (FSO), and Radio Frequency (RF) co-operative communication is of great interest for the researchers. Further these days, the conventional analog and digital relays are replaced by Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS). The realistic channel fading model suitable for FSO communication is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma-\Gamma$</tex> distributions where-as for RF transmissions, it is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa-\mu$</tex> distribution. In this work, we have developed algorithms for calculate the symbol error rate for various phase shift keying modulations. It is observed that IRS-assisted RF and FSO communication systems perform better than the conventional relays. In RF communication, the performance of N/2 elements in two surfaces better than the N elements in a surface where as in FSO, N elements perform better than the two N/2 elements.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Metasurface Antenna for Compact 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This study investigates the design, creation, and implementation of a metasurface antenna (MSA) specifically engineered for 5G connectivity. The MSA is constructed in conjunction with a simple microstrip patch antenna, yielding a realized gain of 4.5 dBi. This is achieved by utilizing a substrate made of Rogers RT Duroid 5880 at a frequency of 25.8 GHz. Elevating the design further, a two-layer 4×4 order metasurface (MS) is introduced, resulting in a substantial gain enhancement to 9.91 dBi. The antenna's dimensions are specified as 0.6 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.6 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.5 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> represents the free space wavelength at 25.8 GHz. The overall 4×4 MSA showcases an impressive maximum efficiency of 86% at the aforementioned frequency. The exceptional performance of the proposed antenna presents a promising trajectory for future 5G implementations, adeptly addressing the multifaceted demands of diverse applications in the realm of next-generation wireless networks.

articleTitle: Bistatic U-Slot Microstrip Patch Antenna for Dual-Band In-Band Full-Duplex
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper implements an in-band full-duplex (IBFD) bistatic microstrip patch antenna with a U-slot for dual-band wireless communication. Two inset feed U-slot microstrip patch antennas, for transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx), are placed orthogonally, separated by a small distance, and a set of shorting vias are inserted along the Rx antenna's radiating edge in-between the antennas. In this compact layout, top-to-bottom connected vias are used to make the antenna a short-circuited quarter-wave resonator and minimize the mutual coupling between the antennas. Tx and Rx antennas have an isolation of −44 dB and −24 dB at 2.12 GHz and 5.28 GHz, respectively. Tx antenna has radiation directivity of 5.19 dBi and 6.33 dBi at 2.12 GHz and 5.28 GHz, respectively. The gain of the Rx antenna in the direction of maximum radiation is 4.91 dBi and 4.42 dBi at 2.12 GHz and 5.28 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Loaded 3D Stacked Antenna for Microwave Imaging of the Human Head
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A metamaterial (MM) loaded compact, flexible, stacked antenna is presented for a portable, low-cost, non-invasive microwave head imaging (MHI) system. The operating frequency of the antenna is 1.81 – 5.4 GHz. The antenna also achieves a peak gain of 5.54 dBi at a frequency of 4 GHz. The optimization of MM unit cell is performed to increase the operational bandwidth, realized gain, and efficiency of the antenna within the bandwidth. The designed compact antenna will be used to image brain cancer at a later stage. All the performance characteristics of the proposed structure were carefully examined from the simulator.

articleTitle: SAR Analysis of a Wearable Textenna for Health Care Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This study delves into the innovative use of various materials—such as denim, cotton, jeans, leather, and silk—as foundational components in antenna design. Specifically tailored for biomedical and healthcare purposes, an original textile antenna built on a denim substrate functions within the 2.4363GHz–2.5236GHz frequency range, precisely centered at 2.47GHz. This antenna exhibits an impressive gain of 6dB and an efficiency nearing 65%, making it exceptionally well-suited for healthcare applications. Leveraging the CST Tool, we conducted meticulous simulations and subsequently fabricated the recommended antenna. Comprehensive testing procedures were employed, including rigorous assessments of the antenna's flexibility, complemented by an exhaustive analysis of its Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) values. This multifaceted approach ensured a thorough evaluation of the antenna's performance characteristics, addressing both its mechanical adaptability and its impact on human tissue in terms of SAR.

articleTitle: A Three-Ray Path Loss Model with Polarization Effects for Indoor Single-Input Single-Output Millimeter-Wave Channel Modelling Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: An accurate and least complexity millimeter-wave three-ray pathloss model with polarization effects was developed for indoor SISO scenarios and implemented in MATLAB. The TE polarized pathloss had larger variations than the TM polarized one. Then, validation using ray tracing gave path losses in an indoor corridor with median differences of 3.016 dB LOS, 1.873 dB NLOS floor, and 2.286 dB NLOS roof. Next, the model was also validated using MoM. This simulations gave mean path loss errors from 2–7 percent of the MoM mean path losses. The path loss was more accurate with TM polarization. Our model is innovative in that- it explicitly incorporates polarization effects; it is less complex, faster, and cheaper than MoM and ray tracing; it does not need large number of meshes and rays; it has no expensive skill and time requirements. Hence, it is suitable for low complexity and low cost applications such as wireless sensor link budget and node location computations.

articleTitle: A Sparse Concentric Ring Antenna Array Design with Wide Scanning and Low Sidelobe Level
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a deterministic synthesis methodology for sparse concentric ring antenna arrays using Bessel functions' approach. Few important design guidelines are brought out to design these antenna arrays. The electromagnetic tool, Ansys HFSS is used to carry out electromagnetic experiment to validate the design technique using a practical radiating element, cavity backed microstrip patch antenna. The design shows wide scan characteristics, low mutual coupling and low side lobe level with uniform excitations being fed to the array. The works is quite useful for phased array antenna applications.

articleTitle: Design of Triangular Shaped Multiple Input Multiple Output Antenna with Defected Substrate for 5G Sub 6 GHz and WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A novel two-element triangular shaped microstrip antenna with defected substrate is presented. The work mentions the design of a novel MIMO (multiple input multiple output) system employing polarization diversity in order to get considerable amount of isolation meeting the requirements of current wireless communication scenario. The antenna works in the band 4.4 to 5.7 GHz thus enabling it to be conveniently used for covering N79 (4.4 to 5.0 GHz) and most of WLAN (5.15 to 5.85 GHz) bands enabling it suitable for 5G sub: 6 GHz applications. A defected substrate is utilized in order to get the lesser coupling between the antennas (−15 dB). The obtained isolation using the proposed antenna is in close proximity to current standards of MIMO devices and suitable to most of the wireless applications. The improved isolation is achieved using the compact dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$21.37 \text{mm}\times 37\text{mm}\times 1.6\ \text{mm}$</tex> with two antenna elements placed orthogonally. The antenna gives gain varying between 3.2 dBi to 5 dBi with radiation efficiency more than 80% in the entire working region.

articleTitle: A Broad Impedance Bandwidth with Dual Sense Triple Band Circular Polarized Printed Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A broad impedance bandwidth with a triple band circularly polarized (CP) slotted rectangular printed monopole antenna is presented in this paper. The designed antenna produces a dual-sense of CP radiation with a satisfactory axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) within the range of impedance bandwidth (IBW). The following results are achieved using a rectangular slotted radiator and a modified partial ground plane. The rectangular slotted radiator consists of two diagonal cuts and one diagonal slut. Modified partial ground contains one equisized stub and slot. The proposed antenna provides -10 dB broad IBW of 10.2 GHz (3.7GHz - 13.9GHz, 116%) while triple bands ARBW of 4.1 GHz (3.67 GHz - 7.75 GHz, 73.87%), 0.5 GHz (9.3 GHz - 9.8 GHz, 5.23%) and 1.3 GHz (12.6 GHz -13.9 GHz, 9.81 %) simultaneously. The radiation efficiency is found more than 90% within the resulting ARBW. This proposed antenna is suitable for ultra-wideband (UWB), S-band and Ku- band applications.

articleTitle: Circular Polarized Conformal Array Antenna For Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A novel flexible array antenna is suggested for satellite applications operating in C- band. This antenna makes use of four patch elements, all of which are connected through independent feed lines to a single coaxial feed. The thickness of the substrate is 1.6 millimetres, and the antenna measures 74.4×74.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. As a substrate, polyamide is utilized, It has a bandwidth of 400 MHz and resonating frequencies at 4.2 GHz. The suggested antenna managed to reach a maximum gain of 5.7 dB while maintaining an efficiency of 85% in its radiation.

articleTitle: Equalization of RMC R.4 Signals using MMSE and Zero Forcing Equalization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Modern wireless communication systems frequently employ the digital modulation method known as orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM). It divides the available bandwidth into several orthogonal subcarriers to deliver high data speeds and effective spectrum usage. However, because to the vulnerability of OFDM systems to numerous channel imperfections, equalizers are used to enhance communication performance and reliability. By adjusting for channel distortions, lowering ISI, and enhancing the precision of symbol recovery, equalizers are essential in OFDM systems. In the face of channel impairments, they are crucial for achieving dependable and high-throughput data transmission. This Paper illustrates the equalization of receiver using two different techniques Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) and Zero Forcing (ZF) equalizers by configuring a cell-wide structure and generating a transmit signal. A propagation channel is configured with specified parameters, including delay profile, number of receiving antennas, and Doppler frequency. It then introduces noise to the signal and simulates multipath Rayleigh fading. Subsequently, it visualizes the received and equalized grids, facilitating a comprehensive analysis of the equalization process. Researchers and practitioners interested in LTE communication systems, channel estimation, and equalization strategies can utilize this paper for a focused investigation into the performance of the MMSE equalizer on LTE R.4 configurations, offering a valuable resource for further analysis and optimization.

articleTitle: A Review on Microwave Imaging for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Breast cancer stands out as the most frequently identified form of cancer and remains the primary contributor to cancer-related fatalities among women globally. Presently, the most effective strategies for managing and treating this disease involve breast scanning for early detection. Within the spectrum of different imaging techniques for breast tumor detection, microwave imaging (MI) is gaining considerable attention as a promising diagnostic tool. MI offers a noninvasive, cost-effective, rapid, user-friendly, and secure screening option. This paper aims to present an updated examination of the principles, advancements, and the ongoing research trends surrounding MI for breast cancer detection.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Shadow Removel and Pavement Crack Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The difficult challenge at hand is automatic pavement crack identification, which involves preserving pavement stability by eliminating shadows that impede fracture detection performance and have the same intensity as cracks. To address the interference caused by shadows, effective algorithm models and training datasets are still lacking. Methodology involves three steps first preprocessing steps improves quality of the image. Second step involves detection of both shadows and removal of shadows whereas in step three classification of cracks is done by using deep learning approach. The system uses intensity values for precision and support multiple image formats. Advanced filtering eliminates noise. Binarizing and filling holes improves crack detection by using cany edge detection. To isolate important features, insignificant blobs are removed and cracks are identified by using feature extraction network. We suggest a data augmentation technique based on this process, which takes into account the variations in brightness brought about by weather and seasonal variations. In the end, we implemented a residual feature augmentation to find tiny fissures that might foretell unexpected catastrophes, and the approach enhances the model's overall performance. Finally, we introduced an deep learning method for classification of cracks that can predict sudden disasters. The system detects cracks at 94% with least MSE. The testing and training accuracy of the proposed model out performs the other state of art methods.

articleTitle: Employing Efficient Decoding Algorithms to Reduce Bit Error Rates in 5G Applications and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In 5G and 6G systems, Bit Error Rate (BER) is a critical performance metric for evaluating the dependability and data transmission quality of communication networks. In order to lower BER values, particularly in challenging channel conditions, 5G and 6G systems employ advanced algorithms. These systems commonly employ error-correcting codes like Turbo codes, Polar codes, or LDPC (Low-Density Parity-Check) codes. These next-generation wireless networks can only meet their stringent BER criteria with the aid of adaptive modulation and coding, and Massive Input & Massive Output (MIMO) techniques. In this paper, the bit error rates for various error correction codes, including BCH (Bose Chaudhuri Hocquenghem),Reed Solmon (RS) Codes LDPC, Turbo, and Polar Codes, have been compared. The entire simulation is carried out using MATLAB.

articleTitle: Simulation and Design for Sub-THz Spectrum TWT Pierce Source with Beam Stabilizer and Magnetic Field Guard
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The design and optimization of a Pierce source with beam stabilizer system tailored for high-power sub-THz traveling-wave tubes (TWTs). The initial parameters for the Pierce-type thermionic electron gun were synthesized using the Vaughan approach. Subsequent optimization was carried out using the MWS CST solver, focusing on a beam voltage of 20 kV. The desired beam radius and beam current density were achieved after 40 iterations of beam area compression. Additionally, a compact periodic permanent magnet system (PPM) was meticulously designed to facilitate the seamless transport of the electron beam. Simulation results demonstrated an impressive 100 % beam transmission through the designated beam tunnel, achieved with an optimum peak magnetic field of 0.25 T. This comprehensive approach underscores the efficacy and potential of our designed electron optics system for high-power sub-THz TWT applications.

articleTitle: Design and Realization of Cascaded S Band Power Amplifier on Hybrid Multilayer PCB
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper a three stage cascaded S band Power Amplifier(PA) is presented. To create a compact module surface mount matched devices are used. In this design 59dB gain with peak output power of 44dBm(25W) is realized on a hybrid multilayer PCB consisting of Teflon and FR4 core materials. The cascaded PA is designed to achieve optimization of size, weight and power. This design is primarily for transmit section of T/R module in Active Phased Array application. The design is tested for −10°C low temperature to +55°C high temperature environments.

articleTitle: 60-GHz Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna-Based Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna is designed to operate in the 65–71 GHz, which is of high interest for fifth- and future-generation wireless applications. The ME dipole exhibits 9 dBi gain, 90% efficiency, high front to back ratio, and identical E- and H-plane patterns. Furthermore, a 60-dB cross-polarization ratio is achieved thanks to a differential feeding based on a TE20 mode generator in a substrate-integrated-waveguide. Within a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> array configuration, a cross-polarization ratio of 20 dB is maintained for various scanning directions of the main beam. Throughout the operating band, the array efficiency is more than 80%.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of RF Energy Harvester for Wearable Sensor Nodes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work, an RF energy harvester to power the wireless sensor nodes, which are embedded with biomedical devices, has been designed. A microstrip antenna with a rectangular patch, inverted U slot in the ground plane, and microstrip fed line is proposed for Wi-Fi frequency band operation. The antenna has an overall size of 54.8 × 49.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>; it is designed on the flexible substrate of Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), which has a dielectric constant of 2.7. The L-section impedance matching circuit is used for the proposed rectenna in the operating band. The designed rectenna is analyzed and simulated in the CST simulator and achieved the return loss < -40 dB and peak realized gain of 4.42 dB at 2.45 GHz resonating frequency with 65% radio frequency signal to DC signal conversion efficiency with 0 dBm input power. The proposed receiver antenna with designed rectifier circuit is capable to powered low power-sensor nodes and low-power wearable devices.

articleTitle: Deployment Mechanisms for Reflectors, Booms, and Feeds Across JPL Missions and Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper explores the critical role of deployable mechanisms in enabling spacecraft missions that demand large radio frequency (RF) aperture systems. Our focus centers on deployable antenna elements, specifically reflectors, booms, and feeds, for which JPL held responsibility in the last decade, addressing their impact on past, present, and future missions. The deployable systems are divided by maturity, starting with successful past deployments, upcoming missions nearing launch, projects in the funded phase without fabricated hardware, and pioneering technologies under development. This paper highlights the innovative accomplishments on deployable RF systems at JPL, from CubeSats to flagship missions. A key theme emerges from the study of these deployable systems: a constant decrease in stowed volume available, and a constant increase in frequency at which the antennas must work and antenna size. This increases the mechanical demands on stowing efficiency and deployment accuracy.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Human Sweat on the Performance of Frequency-Reconfigurable Textenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This study presents a thorough performance evaluation of a versatile wearable antenna capable of frequency and polarisation reconfiguration. The antenna employs a distinctive sickle-shaped primary radiating element complemented by a similar structure serving as the ground component. The antenna design was devised on jute fabric, and the conductivity was achieved through the application of conductive copper paint. Two PIN diodes within the ground plane enable the antenna to function across four configurations. Operating autonomously, the developed antenna functions at 2.4, 4.29, 5.78, and 9.39 GHz in Configuration-1, 5 and 5.9 GHz in Configuration-2, 4.4, and 5.8 GHz in Configuration-3, and finally 3.5, 4.4, and 5.3 GHz in Configuration-4. These reconfigurable textile antennas hold significant promise in various strategic applications, notably in health monitoring, security, and safety. The unique design utilising natural fiber material aims at optimal functionality when in contact with the human body under diverse conditions, including sweat absorption and dust resistance. The experimental investigation scrutinises the antenna's operational performance in simulated sweating circumstances using a synthetic sweat solution. Remarkably, the antenna exhibited consistent performance across all experimental conditions. This underscores the robustness of the ‘textenna,’ a term coined to denote the antenna's reliance on natural jute fiber as a substrate and a traditional brush painting method for its fabrication.

articleTitle: AathreyaSat: A CanSat Model for Air Pollution Measurement in Competition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A CanSat mission, such as the AathreyaSat in the World CanSat/Rocketry Championship (WCRC) competition in Serbia, involves condensing all satellite hardware and software subsystems into a compact container, similar in size to a soda can. These missions serve as valuable learning experiences for students, providing insight into satellite systems and space understanding. The AathreyaSat was designed to be lightweight yet resilient, with specific dimensions of 115mm in height, 66mm in diameter, and a maximum weight of 150 grams. The satellite successfully achieved the WCRC's objectives, which included measuring air pollution during its descent. Notably, the analysis revealed that carbon monoxide levels remained constant throughout the descent, while both humidity and temperature experienced slight increases. This competition fostered innovation and problem-solving skills among participants, enabling them to plan, design, and execute space missions on a smaller scale.

articleTitle: Metasurface-based Frequency Reconfigurable two-port MIMO Antenna for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work metasurface based frequency reconfigurable two-port multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna is presented. Initially, the proposed antenna is configured as a single-port radiating patch with pin-diode operating in the frequency reconfigurable mode. Later the designed antenna is converted to a two-port MIMO antenna that realizes an S11 below -10 dB intended for two resonant bands operating at 2.95 GHz (2.71-3.33 GHz) and 4.91 GHz (4.48-5.24 GHz) with pin-diode off-mode and 3.69 GHz (2.60-4.79 GHz) in on-mode with maximum peak realized gain of 6.29 dB and 4.13 dB at diode off-mode and 9.84 dB in diode on-mode. The two feeding ports of the proposed antenna are positioned adjacent to each other to permit the antenna in self-isolation mode later metasurface-reflector is placed below 10mm of radiator used as a de-coupling circuit and maintaining the minimum isolation of (S21) below -18.5 dB and maximum isolation of -23.07 dB in off-mode and -20.48 dB in diode on-mode. Moreover, the isolation and peak realized gain has improved after adding a reflector to the proposed antenna. The distance between antenna elements is 0.04 λo. The designed antenna is applicable for 5G new radio (NR) bands of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n7$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n48$</tex>, n77, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n78$</tex> in on-mode, and n79 in diode off-mode respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Flexible Substrate-Based Multi-band Patch Antenna for 5G and Satellite Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This research introduces and investigates flexible, cost-effective patch antenna tailored for 5G and Satellite Communication applications. These antennas utilize a polyimide substrate for their flexibility. The compact size of these antennas measures 25mm × 25mm × 0.2 mm. The patch and ground elements of these antennas are structured in circular forms, with deliberate modifications made to achieve concentric shapes in the radiating structures. Operating at frequencies of 2.2GHz, 2.8GHz, 3.4GHz, and 6.3GHz, the polyimide antenna demonstrates suitability for various applications such as weather radar, LTE 5G, and WiMAX. Specifically designed as a flexible monopole antenna, it holds potential for seamless integration into forthcoming flexible electronics dedicated to 5G and Satellite communication bands across the aforementioned frequencies (2.2, 2.8, 3.4, and 6.3 GHz).

articleTitle: High Gain Metamaterial Antenna for High Data Rate Mm-Wave Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a high gain metamaterial based antenna for high data rate millimeter wave communication systems. The frequency band from 37 GHz – 42 GHz can also be used for high data rate communications. The proposed antenna consists of a radiating patch with a metamaterial superstrate layer and is designed over a thin dielectric to provide transmission in the proposed high data rate frequency band. The compact structure with good characteristics in terms of impedance bandwidth (38-40 GHz), antenna gain (>10 dB), return loss (23 dB) (reflection coefficient), reduced losses and high efficiency (95 %) provides a good antenna option to be integrated with the millimeter wave communication systems for high data rate transmissions This electronic document is a “live” template and already defines the components of your paper [title, text, heads, etc.] in its style sheet.

articleTitle: Compact Narrow-Band Sharp Rejection Bandstop Filter Using U-Shaped Resonator for GNSS Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: An U-shaped resonator based bandstop filter (BSF) has been reported in this paper to reject the high power unwanted signal or interfere near to the desired signal. The BSF uses mixed coupling technique - electrical and magnetic - to realize its performance. The U-shaped resonators which are open on both sides are coupled to the feed-line or main line using a coupling gap. The resonators are approximately half-wavelength at the desired frequency of the BSF. As the RF signal passes through the filter the U -shaped resonator selectively captures the particular frequency and allows other frequencies to appear at the output. The mode analysis has been performed to understand the behavior of the circuit. To demonstrate the concept, a bandstop filter rejecting two undesired signals at 1.30 GHz and 1.35 GHz has been designed and fabricated. The filter allows to pass L1 and L5 frequencies with lower insertion loss.

articleTitle: Polarization-Insensitive Metasurface-Biosensor for Glycosuria Sensing in Terahertz Regime
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work presents a single band metasurface perfect absorber (MPA) with a sharp absorption peak. The MPA resonates at 11.912 THz and provides a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 0.353% (BW = 0.042 THz), corresponding to 90% absorptivity. Gold has been used as a material to design top metasurface patterns. The symmetricity in the design leads to polarization-insensitivity with respect to incident plane wave. At the same time, the MPA provides a similar absorptivity response under both transverse electric and transverse magnetic polarizations due to the excitation of the orthogonal modes. Further, MPA has been examined for biosensing, i.e., Glycosuria, in this work. For the 0.002 change in the value of the refractive index (n), a 0.0002 THz change in resonance frequency has been observed (Sensitivity = 100 GHz/RIU), which confirms the efficacy of the proposed MPA for biosensing in the terahertz regime.

articleTitle: A Rectangular Slotted Symmetrical Antenna for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a rectangular slotted planar antenna is proposed for WLAN applications. The structure consists of eight rectangular slots and the structure is symmetrical about y-axis along with reflectors. An insert feed technique is used for impedance matching. The antenna resonates at 5.2GHz with an impedance bandwidth of 200 MHz's. The reflectors are surrounded from three sides to direct the beam in the broadside direction. The measured directivity of the proposed antenna is 7.37 dB. A comparison with existing antennas at the same frequency is also tabulated.

articleTitle: A 3-bit Intelligent Reflective Surface with Reconfigurable Phase States, Polarization Insensitivity and Angular Stability for Wi-Fi and IoT applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This article involves the design and analysis of a novel unit cell designed for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces(RIS) based on metasurfaces operating at 5.8GHz for Wi-Fi and IoT applications. The unit cell consists of a circular loop antenna-inspired structure printed on top of a 1.58mm Taconic TLY substrate which is ground plane-backed. A biasing grid is placed around the loop and a center via is placed connecting the ground plane to the top of the structure. The inner circular loop is designed in such a way as to have more reflection from the surface. The EM simulation of the metasurface is performed and the results are presented in which the 8 distinct phase states with average reflection loss of 1.67 dB are clear. The proposed design is found to be polarization insensitive concerning linear polarization. Also, the angular stability of the structure is tested and works well with fair results till 40°incident angles. The periodicity used here is 25mm. The results are pleasant looking and found to be suitable for Wi-Fi and IoT applications that use the 5.8 GHz - ISM band of frequencies.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Band Monopole Antenna for Internet of Things and Sub-6 GHz 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A compact dual-band monopole antenna is proposed for the Internet of Things (IoT) and Sub-6 GHz band 5G applications. The proposed antenna is comprised of a simple inverted C-shaped tapered microstrip line and partial ground. The overall FR4 substrate dimensions are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$40\ \text{mm}\ \times\ 12\ \text{mm}\ \times\ 1.6 \text{mm}$</tex>. The antenna is designed and optimized in the Ansys HFSS tool. The inverse C-shaped microstrip line radiates from 4.8 GHz to 5.7 GHz and the L-shaped microstrip line radiates from 2.3 GHz to 2.6 GHz at higher and lower bands. The proposed antenna demonstrates enhanced performance in terms of reflection coefficient (<−10dB), radiation patterns, peak gain (2.7 at 2.4 GHz and 1.8 at 5.2 GHz), and radiation efficiency (95% at 2.4 GHz and 93% at 5.2 GHz). The results of the prototype test show significant correlations with the simulation results. The novel, compact antenna is able to be combined with IOT sensors, RF modules at the frequency of 2.4 GHz (ISM band) and sub-6 bands for 5G WLAN applications.

articleTitle: Compact Water-Based Coaxial Delay Line
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The coaxial cables are commonly used as delay lines in phased arrays for steering the antenna beam in the sky. At low radio frequencies, larger array size and element spacings necessitate use of longer delay lines for phasing, resulting in networks of unmanageable dimensions. This problem could be overcome by realizing lines on high dielectric constant medium. We have developed a water based composite dielectric medium which has an effective dielectric constant of ∼ 40. A coaxial cable of about 22cm long has been constructed using it. Its insertion loss varies from 0.5 dB to 2.5 dB and reflection coefficient is better than 10 dB over 30–360 MHz band. Its delay characteristic is shown to be equal to that of a 1m long teflon-based cable, demonstrating the reduction of cable length by a factor of 4.5 through the use of a high dielectric constant composite medium. The cable parameters have been optimized and a prototype has been built to validate the design.

articleTitle: Model-Based Design for Direction-Finding with Amplitude Comparison
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Direction-finding is used in many applications to locate the source of RF emissions and microwave signals. Direction-finding can be done using analog or digital techniques. This paper discusses analog implementation using amplitude comparison. The model in this paper is built using RF Blockset, and the antenna is integrated with the RF channel to simulate an entire system. Amplitude comparison can be achieved using many different antenna configurations and array architectures. A rectangular array is used at the receiver in this paper, and the antenna beam is scanned achieving the maximum power and detect the angle of arrival. The model offers rapid antenna and RF component prototyping, and different scenarios can be simulated very easily. The model also considers impedance mismatches between the blocks so the power transmitted and received can be accurately modelled.

articleTitle: Reflector Antennas Design and Analysis Software
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Reflector antennas are commonly used in the satellite applications and need careful design for obtaining high efficiency values. Especially multibeam and array fed reflectors require multiple iterations to obtain the optimal dimensions, which could be time consuming with the full wave simulations. This paper presents a software developed using gaussian beam analysis for quick initial design of the reflector antennas. Multiple feed types have been discussed, including single horn feeds, array feeds and feed clusters for multiple beams.

articleTitle: Varactor Tunable Compact MIMO Antenna with Reconfigurable Multi Band Operating and Notching for Cognitive Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This article presents a compact planar MIMO antenna configuration incorporating electronic tunability to create band notched functionality for ultra wideband (UWB) applications. The initial design features a partially grounded, modified rectangular monopole to exhibit UWB characteristics. The characteristics of band notch are realized by employing a meander line that is loaded to the rectangular monopole and a U-shaped slot etched along the feedline. The proposed antenna offers an exceptionally wide operating range spanning from 3 to 11 GHz, featuring notched frequencies at 5.6 and 7.6 GHz. To enhance the antenna's versatility, these notched frequencies are electronically adjusted by incorporating two varactor diodes. Furthermore, the antenna provides operating bands spanning from 4.1 GHz to 4.4 GHz, 5.8 to 7.4 GHz, and 8.7 to 12 GHz. The suggested MIMO antenna possesses a total size of 38 x 38 x 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: $4\times 4$ Planar Antenna Array for Enhanced Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper introduces an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> Planar Array for Enhanced gain within the frequency range of 3.2 GHz to 4.5 GHz. The antenna occupies a space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$60.5\times 60.5\times 1.6$</tex>. The antenna configuration, optimized for broadband performance, enables spatial diversity, offering enhanced reliability and increased data rates. The proposed design demonstrates its efficacy in the 3.2 GHz–4.5 GHz frequency band, and the gain of the antenna is 6.4 dB which helps in catering to the evolving needs of wireless communication networks.

articleTitle: Design of a 4-element UWB-MIMO Antenna for X,Ku, and, K Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The 4-port MIMO antenna structures designed in this paper have the following benefits: low profile, straightforward development, excellent isolation, peak gain, efficiency, and return loss. The characteristics of performance are observed for the proposed mechanisms for design by slotting the meander line of the latter two shapes at the patch, adding the stair shapes at the two bottom edges of the patch, and cutting the rectangle slot in the ground plane. The antenna has a -45 dB least reflection coefficient, isolation of more than 50dB, ECC lower than 0.0040, CCL is less than 0.2 bps/Hz, a total gain of 6 dBi, efficiency is about 75%. A wideband analysis of the proposed approach is conducted covering the frequency spectrum of 1 GHz to 20 GHz. The suggested work is appropriate for the wireless applications in the UWB/X/Ku/K bands owing to its multiple band responses.

articleTitle: Adaptive Filter Clipper-Based PAPR Reduction Techniques for Massive MIMO-OFDM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) is a critical issue in Massive–MIMO OFDM systems as it increases power consumption. The channel state interference (CSI) is another significant effect in Massive MIMO-OFDM considering wide base stations deployed on measured areas. The research work proposed in this paper mainly deals with various PAPR-OFDM reduction techniques based on computational complexity, bandwidth expansion, spectrum leakage, and performance. In this paper, algorithms that simultaneously achieve multiuser interference (MUI) elimination and PAPR reduction are developed. An enhancement aid approach to reduce the PAPR of the transmitted signal has been suggested by adding a carefully designed synthetic disturbance signal to the pre-coded signal.

articleTitle: A Trapezoidal Ground-based Truncated Rectangular Patch Antenna for Non-Invasive Monitoring of Bone Fracture Healing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a truncated rectangular patch antenna is designed for non-invasive monitoring of bone fracture healing. The proposed antenna is developed on the trapezoidal-shaped ground plane with a compact size of 25×25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Rogers RT droid 5880 substrates with 0.25mm thickness. The antenna is simulated, fabricated, and tested by simulating a phantom model. The proposed antenna resonates at 4.8 GHz. The antenna characteristics show S11 of -45 dB, measured 10 dB impedance bandwidth of 1.2 GHz (4.4-5.6 GHz), shifted results at 3.9 GHz in the presence of phantom, and measured maximum gain of 3.4 dBi. For non-invasive monitoring of bone fracture healing, the proposed antenna shows an average linear sensitivity of 4 MHz/εr.

articleTitle: Analysis of Uniform Amplitude Butler Beam Forming Network for X/Ku-Band for Air-Borne Synthetic Aperture Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this article, the signal processing technique known as beamforming is discussed in relation to a number of industries, such as telecommunications, wireless communication systems, radar, sonar, and acoustics. The recommended frequencies for the Ku band at 13.265 GHz and the X band at 9. 3GHz.Couplers, crossovers, and phase shifters are produced as a result of the components, which are utilised to realise the design of beamforming networks. Insertion loss for the proposed crossover is less than 2dB. Butler matrix-based beamforming network with substrate with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}{=2.2}$</tex>, height <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=0.8$</tex> mm with 8 different beamforms at- 20°,-15°,-10°,-5°,5°,10°, 15°,200. the theoretically predicted total power of 9.030dB, By merging various signals or waveforms to create a concentrated, directional beam, beamforming networks (also known as Butler matrices) can theoretically increase power by amplifying the targeted signal and eliminating interference and noise from other directions. The significance of beamforming is found in its capacity to enhance signal quality. By reducing route loss and attenuations, beamforming increases communication range and quality. Target localisation depends heavily on beamforming.

articleTitle: LoRa - Powered Smart Agriculture System for Monitoring and Controlling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: As the technology advances the traditional farming is heading towards smart agriculture. In smart agriculture the various parameters like soil moisture levels, temperature, humidity, and presence like NH3, CO2 etc., at field and crops are analyzed. This data from sensors is communicated to microcontroller for necessary processing and action. Usually, data is communicated using internet. But in rural and extreme regions where internet is not available and has poor connectivity then communication wont possible. In these cases, Long Range Network (LoRa) can be optimum communication technique. LoRa technique provides low cost and effective communication network without use of internet. In this work LoRa based smart agriculture system is implemented. The sensors located in farmland distanced at few Kilometers are communicated and operated using LoRa. The system monitors temperature, humidity and gases in real time and automatically controls water level in farms by enabling the features of smart irrigation system. The prototype of LoRa transmitter and receiver are developed that works without internet.

articleTitle: Dual-Band, Dual-Polarized Reconfigurable Reflectarray Antenna Operating at C and X Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dual-band, dual-polarized reconfigurable reflectarray antenna designed to operate efficiently in the C and X bands. The unit cell design comprises two square rings, each consisting of four varactor diodes for dynamic reconfigurability. A notable simplification in biasing circuitry is achieved by applying a consistent bias voltage across the varactor diodes in both rings. The unit cell achieves a continuous phase range of 310° and 309° at 5.55 GHz and 10 GHz, respectively, with peak losses of 0.78 dB and 0.65 dB. Preliminary simulation results show a consistent beam steering capability with a gain of around 21 dB and 24 dB at C and X band respectively. Due to the inherent symmetry in the unit cell structure, the proposed antenna can operate with both x- and y-polarized incident waves.

articleTitle: LTCC Based Microstrip Antenna Designed for Millimeter Wave Applications Using CPW-Fed Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a CPW-fed wideband microstrip antenna with multilayered technology. It is proposed for millimeter-wave applications at 60GHz (V-band). The antenna consists of six layered substrate ESL41111-G of size 3mm×2.8mm with relative permittivity of 4.11. It consists of octagonal shaped patch on top of top layer and a periodic structure on the second layer of the substrate. The technique utilized to design antenna is called Low Temperature Co-Fired Ceramic (LTCC), which is 3D multilayer structure integrated vertically. The proposed antenna operates over the frequency range of 58-62GHz with bandwidth of 11.2% and has a gain of 3.5dB. The antenna has advantages of simple fabrication, process without using integrated cavities, vias, or other complicated structures like AMCs, EBG, SIW, or LTCC-LPC structures. This LTCC-based broadband antenna is designed using HFSS and the simulation's findings show a lot of promises in wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: X-Band Rugged Remotely Monitored Controller Based High Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper describes the design and development of of a Gallium Nitride (GaN) based Solid State Pulsed Power Amplifier (SSPPA). Pulsed Power amplifiers are the main building blocks for all pulsed RADAR systems. This paper dwells on the design of the RF section and an innovative design of a microcontroller and multivibrator based circuits to monitor, display and protect high power solid state amplifiers. This amplifier works in the X-band, generating a peak pulsed power of 50W, up to a duty cycle of 20%. This amplifier can be used as a basic building block to realize higher power amplifiers, which can replace microwave tubes.

articleTitle: A Moon Shaped Slotted Pentagonal Patch Antenna with DGS for High-Gain and X Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a pentagonal patch antenna designed for high-gain applications is presented, with a moon-shaped slot. The proposed pentagonal patch antenna dimensions are 40x40x1.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. A pentagonal patch antenna with a circular slot resulted in dual-band operation with a bandwidth of 210MHz (9.49GHz-9.70GHz) and 200MHz (9.49GHz-9.69GHz) with a peak gain of 8.0dBi at 9.55GHz. A moon shape slot resulted in single-band with a bandwidth of 200MHz (9.50GHz to 9.70GHz) with a peak gain of 8.2dBi at 9.64GHz. To improve the gain and bandwidth of the proposed antenna, DGS is introduced in the ground plane. Simulations were done using ANSYS HFSS software.

articleTitle: Multi Slot Wearable Patch Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a Wearable Rectangular Patch Antenna (WRAP) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.1\text{GHz}$</tex> wireless communications applications. The cotton is employed as substrate to be easily integrated with wearable clothes like baggage, dress, belt hand strips etc. The antenna is Compact in size with a dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$32{\text{\ mm\ }} \times \ 42{\text{\ mm}}$</tex> slotted rectangular geometry. The designed antenna has an operating frequency of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.1\text{GHz}$</tex>. The antenna has gain of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.7\text{dBi}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.3\text{GHz}$</tex> bandwidth with good radiation pattern. The designed antenna has medical, IoT and 5G applications.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Polarization Transforming Metasurface for Multiband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Crafted with precision, the Metasurface (MS) skillfully converts linear polarization to circular polarization. It has an orthotropic structure with two symmetrical axes (u and v) that are at right angles to the vertical y-axis and precisely perpendicular to one another. Operating frequencies with an impression range of 5.2-2.57 GHz, 7.7-8 GHz, and 10.8-11.2 GHz. This MS is ideal for tactical radar and communication systems operating in the C and X bands. Because of its anisotropic nature, which causes its properties to change depending on direction, it can withstand waves coming in at an oblique angle and yet remain stable. It is actually able to continue working at angles as high as ±90°, which is important in real-world situations where waves may not always come in at a straight line. This amazing MS justifies its moniker as an ultra-wideband converter since it can effectively transform linearly polarized signals into circular polarized waves over a broad frequency range. Results from simulations and experiments have been presented to demonstrate its efficacy. Impressively, the bandwidth where circular polarization is attained, the 3db axial ratio band, spans a remarkable 2GHz to 14GHz for both x- and y-polarized incidences. This MS is a broadband circular-polarization converter (CPC) in addition to being an excellent polarization converter. Because of its versatility, it is a very popular option for many radar and communications systems.

articleTitle: A Compact Triple Band FSS Based Microstrip Antenna for 2.4/4/5.8 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A novel shaped compact triple band microstrip patch antenna utilizing Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) for improving gain is proposed. The dimension of the proposed FSS based antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.407\lambda_{0}\times 0.407\lambda_{0}\times 0.11\lambda_{0}$</tex> (here free space wavelength is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}$</tex> at 2.407 GHz). Mainly three valuable frequency bands for wireless communication systems are covered by the proposed antenna. The achieved frequency bands are 60 MHz (2380 - 2440 MHz) for 2404 MHz ISM band, 140 MHz (3800 - 3940 MHz) for satellite downlink in UK and 1070 MHz (5700 - 6770 MHz) for ISM band 5801 MHz WiMAX and WLAN applications. The size of the antenna is very small. Obtained gain of the antenna is not sufficient for wireless system. The peak gain is enhanced significantly for utilizing band stop FSS at the back side of the antenna. The peak gain is enhanced to 4.2 dBi, which is 7.5 dBi more than that of simple fabricated antenna. The proposed antenna is also very compact.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Monolithic Feed Assemblies for Satellite Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Cost and schedules are critical to satellite communications payloads. Antenna system represents an important part of the satellite payload, and the design varies from satellite to satellite based on the requirements and type of satellite. Design, fabrication, test and qualification consumes significant schedule due to manufacture of the feed systems meeting tight tolerances and hence increased cost. This paper presents a low-cost manufacturing method of a monopulse feed assembly using 3-D manufacturing. Results presented show that 3-D manufactured feed meets stringent requirements of the monopulse feed including very deep nulls.

articleTitle: Medical Imaging Using a Wideband, Conformal, Textile Antenna for Brain Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work a conformal textile antenna is designed for imaging tumor in the brain. Here, a leaf-shaped patch with shorting pins connected to a circular ring on the back side of the antenna with defected ground is made to achieve the required performance for head imaging. The put forward model operatres from 1.74 to 6.5 GHz. The device obtains a maximum gain of 3.4 dBi. The Specific Absorption rate (SAR) of the designed antenna is checked at several frequencies within the broadband of the antenna. This is done by separately designing a 7 layered head model. All the performance parameters of the put forward structure is studied from the simulator. Also multiple copies of the designed antenna are placed around the modelled head phantom for getting adequate data for imaging the embedded tumor at a later stage.

articleTitle: Advancing Bandpass Filters: Spatio-Temporal Modulation with Coupled Line Sections for Non-Reciprocal Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a microstrip non-reciprocal 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order coupled line bandpass filter by applying time-modulated waves to the half-wavelength resonators. The varactors, loaded into each half-wavelength resonators, are modulated with sinusoidal signals to generate time-varying capacitance superimposed on a nominal capacitance effectuated by reverse-biased DC voltages. By properly introducing progressive phase difference between the modulation waves, circuit analysis shows that non-reciprocal filtering isolation response can be achieved. To validate the suggested approach, a microstrip 3rd-order non-reciprocal bandpass filter based on parallel coupled lines at 2.4 GHz is designed and simulated. Advanced electromagnetic simulation tools were used to run extensive simulations in order to show the effectiveness of the suggested design. The simulated outcomes demonstrate insertion loss less than 4 dB, return loss greater than 10 dB, isolation more than 20 dB with good selectivity and stop band rejection suitable for WLAN applications.

articleTitle: Study Of 5G Adaptive Beamforming in Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: 5G systems are introduced in the modern era to void latency, interference and to increase the system efficiency. But the coexistence in these systems may cause the users data to attack with interference. Hence, to avoid such interferences a linearly constrained least mean square filter is designed. Algorithm for 5G Interference-coexistence communication reduces the mean square error when compared to all other previous methods. Adaptive beamforming is a signal processing technique that improves the signal strength in a particular direction by combining sounds from an array of microphones with specific delays. Adaptive beam-forming uses various algorithms to identify the signals in the desired direction and separate the interference from the undesired/unwanted direction.

articleTitle: Novel Ultra-Miniaturized Wideband Linear-Circular and Linear-Cross Polarizer Based on Modified Electric Dipole Configuration at THz Regime
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper showcases a novel reflection wideband linear-circular and linear-cross polarization converter for THz regime applications. The reflective polarizer design uses a thin, low-loss grounded dielectric substrate with a modified electric dipole. This study uses this approach since reflective polarization converters are inherently wideband performance. The suggested layout converts the EM wave from linear to circular polarization in the following frequency ranges: 0.350-0.365 THz, 0.429-0.747 THz, 1.125-1.803 THz, and 1.972-2.010 THz, all with an Axial Ratio (AR) of at least 3dB. On top of that, it can also perform linear-cross polarization from 0.379-0.404 THz, 0.837-1.010 THz, and 1.868-1.935 THz with a minimum Polarization Conversion Ratio (PCR) of 90%. In addition, the reason behind the wideband simultaneous dual-conversion is investigated after the deep analysis of the electric field and surface current distribution profiles of the multiple plasmonic resonances. With an overall volume of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.088(\lambda_{L}^{3}/1000)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{\mathrm{L}}$</tex> is the free-space wavelength and approximately the lowest working frequency, the suggested unitcell is ultra-miniaturized. The proposed design functionality is examined for the TE and TM modes at various oblique angles. The design's unique selling points are the proposed polarizer compactness and, thanks to multiple wideband linear-cross and linear-circular conversions.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Diversity Techniques in Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The performance, dependability, and general effectiveness of wireless communications, including in 5G networks, are greatly enhanced by Diversity Techniques. In line with the main goals of 5G technology, they assist in addressing issues with fading, interference, and noise as well as improving system capacity, dependability, and spectral efficiency. The performance of several diversity strategies used in wireless communication systems, such as Alamouti coding, maximal-ratio combining, and G4-coded 4×1 systems, is thoroughly analyzed in this work using extensive simulations. The outcomes of our research greatly advance our knowledge of how diversity approaches improve the reliability of data transmission in wireless communication systems. The design and optimization of systems in difficult conditions will benefit greatly from these discoveries, which will ultimately increase overall performance and dependability.

articleTitle: A 2-6GHz Wideband BPF and A Miniaturised Tri-Band BPF Based on HMSIW
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a 2-6GHz wideband and a miniaturised tri-band bandpass filter (BPF) for 5G/6G applications. The wideband BPF is constructed by loading Half Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide (HMSIW) with an inverted L-shaped DGS, achieving fractional bandwidths (FBW) of 125%. The tri-band BPF is implemented using an HMSIW loaded with Complimentary Split Ring Resonators (CSRR) at the top and bottom ground planes, enabling evanescent mode operation below the SIW line's cut-off frequency. The resonators have been optimised to align with the desired frequency bands, resulting in centre frequencies at 2.4GHz, 3.5GHz and 6GHz, with FBW of 9.2%, 1.4% and 32.4%, respectively. The wideband BPF occupies a compact footprint of 0.11 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a triband filter of 0.03λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> is the guided wavelength at the lowest frequency band.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Ku Band Receiver Front End for Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a systemic analysis and measurements of a radiofrequency front-end receiver for satellite communications in Ku Band, as well as the design charac-terization of the first stage, which has a satisfactory a high conversion gain (CG), low-noise figure (NF) to reduce the noise contribution of following stages, and a high linearity to avoid receiver saturation in the presence of interference's. This is the first experimental demonstration of a down converter receiver with high gain and low NF that has been designed and executed. The intended receiver features high conversion gain and good linearity. The planned down converter has a conversion gain of 66 dB and a maximum IF output of 8 dBm. Furthermore, the designed receiver has a minimal NF of 6 dB across its bandwidth.

articleTitle: Exploring ML Solutions for Challenges in WSN Development: A Comprehensive Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Significant challenges with energy and security, which are mutually exclusive, faced by wireless sensor networks. Battery consumption will rise in tandem with an increase in security complexity. Owing to wireless sensor networks' limited power and their dynamic topology, attempts have been made to Common security methods like key management and cryptography are worthless. One of the recommended approaches in this type of system is the use of machine learning algorithms to deliver safety measures by combining intelligence-based decision-making with surveillance. Thus, these dynamic situations can be handled by machine learning algorithms. The security, routing, clustering, that WSNs face are some of the ones that are evaluated against the corresponding problems in this survey paper using machine learning (ML) algorithms. Consequently, this review paper offers a general overview of ML algorithms for various problems encountered by WSN.

articleTitle: A Novel Reconfigurable UWB Antenna for Spectral Sensing and Signal Transmission in Cognitive Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents, an ultrawide band (UWB) hexagonal ring microstrip patch antenna for cognitive radio applications. It comprises of a microstrip line fed, octagonal ring radiator etched on top of FR4 Epoxy substrate with a semi ground plane, consisting of rectangular slit. Frequency reconfiguration is attained using six semiconductor PIN diodes that attach or disconnect the parasitic elements placed near the feed line. Depending on various PIN diode switching arrangements the antenna operates in spectral sensing mode covering the complete UWB range and transmit/ receive mode providing selection of certain frequency bands. Thus, instead of using two separate antennas in cognitive radio systems a single antenna can be used. The proposed compact antenna is simple and is of low cost. It is simulated in CST Microwave Studio, fabricated and validated. The simulation and measured results confirm decent agreement, certifying the suitability for cognitive radio systems front-end.

articleTitle: Significance of Phase Center in Satellite Antenna Designs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Phase center of antennas in design of satellite antenna payloads is an important parameter that could be used to manipulate the antenna radiation patterns. Two design examples are shown, one for reflector antennas and the other for phased arrays, where phase center plays a key role in shaping the antenna radiation patterns to meet the requirements. These include antenna designs with frequency-variant phase center and frequency-invariant phase center.

articleTitle: A Half-Mode SIW Cavity-Backed 3-Ports MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this article, a compact and low-profile rhombus-shaped antenna is designed and extended to a 3-element multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with a defected ground structure (DGS). A reduction in the antenna footprint by 50% is achieved which implies a decrease in the physical area occupied by the antenna to half of its original size, hence Half-mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide (HMSIW) technology is utilized in the proposed antenna. A rectangular slot is etched at the center of the HMSIW cavity which enhances the overall bandwidth of the antenna by 50%. The slot at the center of the cavity splits the dominant TE110 mode of the HM cavity into odd- and even-half TE110 modes in proximity. The antenna resonates around 5.7 GHz and 5.8 GHz in proximity which covers a bandwidth of 200 MHz. The isolation levels between any two radiating elements are improved by a Y-shaped slot in the ground plane, obtained below -20 dB. The overall size of the three-port MIMO antenna is 1.0λgx 0.8λg. The peak gain of the antenna is obtained at 5.9 dBi at a lower resonant frequency and 6.25 dBi at an upper resonant frequency while radiation efficiency is better than 90% in a complete frequency band. The MIMO antenna performance metrics are evaluated theoretically and compared with the simulated results. The envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) is obtained less than 0.015, DG is around 9.9 dBi, and mean effective gain (MEG) is around -3.05 dB.
